payload.description:
## Context

Plan §5A item 2 names `89hm`, `vkh0.23` and `ejdm` as where to start. Measured 2026-08-14 over
`blocks` edges in `.beads/issues.jsonl`, with `parent-child` excluded because a parent epic is
open by construction and is not a blocker:

```text
basicly-89hm      P0  BLOCKED by basicly-u2hl.30 [open]
basicly-vkh0.23   P0  BLOCKED by basicly-c357    [open]
basicly-ejdm      P0  READY
```

Two of the three cannot be started. `basicly-c357` is itself a P0, is READY, and appears nowhere
in plan §6 - which describes the cutover as five steps while the tracker holds its actual entry
point, so only one of the two was read.

Separately, `basicly-jn1x` is a READY P0 that no ordering in the file names. It is a prerequisite
of any measurement citing a role rather than a competitor for a slot: 0 of 357 dispatch records
carry `--agent`, positive control 163 carry `-p`, so the ledger cannot distinguish "the lane path
does not apply the role" from "it does and the record does not capture it".

## The defect

An ordering is a **claim about the dependency graph** and this one was written from the epic
bodies. Both misses are visible in a single query. Nothing gates a plan ordering against the
graph, which is the same shape as `basicly-48d1`, `basicly-pip9` and `basicly-miqr` one layer
over: a document read as fact with no check behind it.

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-tyobdb` made the board state how far its gate verdict lags the document, and mark it stale past a window. **Age is a proxy.** The question a reader actually has is *"was this verdict taken at the head I am looking at"*, and the run artifact records no head.

So the board still cannot tell these two apart:

- a verdict from 20 minutes ago on a tree nobody has touched — **valid**, and now drawn as stale;
- a verdict from 3 minutes ago taken before two merges — **worthless**, and drawn as fresh.

The second is the dangerous one and the first is the noisy one. Both are wrong for the same reason: the artifact says *when* it ran, not *what* it ran against.

## Measured

`.basicly/usage/verify-run.json` holds exactly `mode`, `recorded_at`, `passed`, `checks`. The board's `repo` section already carries `head` and `dirty`, so the consumer has one half of the comparison and the producer never wrote the other.

## Why this is small

`verify_artifact.write_run_artifact` already takes the repo root. `checkout` and `merge` both read the head elsewhere in the tree, so nothing new has to be discovered — the head is one `git rev-parse` the artifact does not currently record, and `board_usage.gates` passes it through.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a verify run is recorded, THE ARTIFACT SHALL carry the commit it verified and whether the tree was dirty at the time.
- WHEN the board draws a verdict taken at a different head from the one it is showing, IT SHALL say which and SHALL NOT draw it in the failing vocabulary.
- WHEN the verdict's head matches, THE AGE ALONE SHALL NOT mark it stale, because an untouched tree does not go stale.
- WHERE the artifact predates this field, THE BOARD SHALL fall back to the age window `basicly-tyobdb` shipped, and say it is doing so.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify_artifact.py`
- `src/basicly/board_usage.py`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `tests/test_verify_artifact.py`
- `tests/test_board_footer.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: Record a verify pass, make a commit, serve the board, and read the gates cell naming the head mismatch rather than a green tree.
payload.title: the verify artifact records when it ran but not what it ran against

## Trigger
When a release checkout carries a local-only earlier version tag, I want the shipped-core inventory and release validation to use a consistent release history, so a published checkout passes the same hash-inventory check as its authoring checkout.

## Scope
- `src/basicly/shipped_core.py`
- `src/basicly/shipped_core.json`
- `tests/test_shipped_core.py`
- `src/basicly/release*.py`
- `changelog.d/**`

## Steps to Reproduce
The v0.26.10 and v0.26.11 committed shipped_core.json files both list v0.26.9. The local repository has that withheld tag, while git ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/v0.26.9 refs/tags/v0.26.10 returns only v0.26.10 (positive control). release_tags_before enumerates local version tags; build_digests folds their core hashes into the packaged inventory. GitHub quality-gates run 39474282454 for 8dd7e629 failed test_the_shipped_hash_list_is_current_with_every_earlier_release_tag: 7193 passed, one failed, one expected failure. The test expected an inventory without v0.26.9. Local full and trial-clone checks passed because they shared the unpublished local tag. The release workflow and fresh-install consumer checks passed. This history mismatch predates the hook recovery fix.

Do not publish the withheld v0.26.9 tag, rewrite a published tag, or weaken the equality check to clear this defect. Establish the intended release-history contract and add a regression using a local-only prior tag before choosing the repair.
payload.requirements: Preserve published release immutability. Do not publish withheld tags or weaken inventory checks.

Use a separate committed canonical published-tag-to-commit input, bootstrapped from origin advertised version tags. payload.description:
## Trigger
The Anthropic prompting audit (2026-09-12) found the `catalog-authoring` skill states "Emphasis is a scarce resource: at most one IMPORTANT-style marker per projection" and no gate enforces it.

## Problem
An unenforced budget drifts. Every marker added makes every other marker weaker, and the drift is invisible until a projection carries several and none of them read as urgent.

## Fix
Count the emphasis markers each target projection composes to, and refuse in `basicly catalog lint` when a projection carries more than one.

## Acceptance
- `catalog lint` refuses a second marker in one projection and names both sites.
- The current tree passes, or the surplus markers are removed in the same change.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a recorded context occupancy greater than the declared window for its runner spec when the check runs then it fails naming both figures and the six existing records are the fixture and a control passes inside the window and the window is declared per agent in config with its source recorded rather than defaulted silently
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
rg -n "_CONTEXT_WINDOWS" src/basicly/runner.py
rg -n "DEFAULT_CONTEXT_CEILING|DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX" src/basicly/config.py
uv run python -c "
import json, pathlib
d = json.loads(pathlib.Path('.basicly/usage/run-records.json').read_text())
for k, v in d.items():
    for r in v:
        if r.get('context_tokens'):
            print(k, r['context_tokens'], r.get('forecast_tokens'))"
```

Observed - `basicly-tcmy.5` recorded a final context occupancy of **223221 tokens** while the
engine declares the claude window as **200000**. Expected - a lane cannot occupy more of a window
than the window has.

## The defect is a stale capability constant, not a sizing error

`context_occupancy` (`runner.py:1592-1601`) is documented as *"how full the model's window was at
the end of the run"* - the last assistant message's own usage on the `claude-stream-json` arm, not a
cumulative sum. So a recorded 223221 is a direct measurement of window occupancy, and it exceeds the
declared window. **The repo's own telemetry refutes `runner.py:119`.**

`_CONTEXT_WINDOWS = {"claude": 200_000, ...}` was written when 200000 was the right figure. The model
this repo now dispatches is Claude Opus 5, whose context window is **1000000** (checked against the
vendor's live model documentation on 2026-08-04, not recalled). The consequence chain:

- `ceiling_tokens` = `context_window * context_ceiling` = `200000 * 0.6` = **120000**
- the true guard, on a 1M window at the same 0.6 fraction, is **600000**
- so the finalize protocol fires at one fifth of its intended point

Seven lanes carry a measured occupancy; six crossed 120000 and **every one is far below 600000**:

| lane | context_tokens | over 120000 | over 600000 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| basicly-tcmy.5 | 223221 | yes | no |
| basicly-gczc | 210721 | yes | no |
| basicly-vkh0.10 | 193096 | yes | no |
| basicly-tcmy.6 | 190177 | yes | no |
| basicly-tcmy.22 | 171029 | yes | no |
| basicly-jr0l.64 | 170530 | yes | no |
| basicly-8ry8 | 80211 | no | no |

**Every one of those six finalizations was spurious.** The tracker holds **twelve**
`(context-ceiling overrun)` follow-up beads, eight still open, and the 2026-08-03 pass shipped four
beads while creating three of them - so `basicly-tcmy.5`, `.6` and `.22` are partial landings whose
remainders (`basicly-tcmy.39`, `.38`, `.37`) exist only because of this constant. At a one-to-one
ship-to-follow-up ratio the release ladder does not converge, which makes this the single highest
-leverage defect open against the factory.

This is the family basicly-z2wi, basicly-3w44, basicly-ipx2 and basicly-tcmy.34 belong to, seen from
a new angle: not a number in the wrong unit, but a number describing a capability the runtime no
longer has. It is also the exact shape of the owner rule that a vendor capability must be read from
the vendor's live documentation rather than recalled - the constant was correct when written and
nothing re-checked it.

## Fix shape

**Do not hardcode 1000000 from the documentation either** - that repeats the original mistake with a
newer number, and a consumer pinning a different model or a 200k session inherits a window we made
up for them. Three parts:

- **Declare the window, per agent, in config.** `runner.py:116` already documents the field as
  config-overridable per agent; this repo declares nothing, so it silently takes the default. Make
  the resolved window a declared, reviewable value, and record on each dispatch which source it came
  from - the same declared-versus-measured discipline `decompose.BUILD_FACTOR_SEED` and
  `forecast_source` already follow.
- **Gate the constant against the ledger.** The contradiction above is mechanically detectable:
  a recorded `context_tokens` greater than the declared window for that spec is a proof the
  declaration is wrong. Add a check that fails on it and names both figures - the same stance the
  evidence-bound ceiling gate already takes, which fired correctly twice on 2026-08-03. Had it
  existed, it would have caught this the first time a lane recorded 210721.
- **Then re-derive the trigger, not the fraction.** `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_CEILING = 0.6` is a behavioural
  guard below the real window (design D8) and is not what is broken; leave it alone. The trigger
  follows from the corrected window.

**A regression test must be proven red first** (basicly-kjc5.49): assert that a run whose recorded
occupancy exceeds the declared window for its spec fails the check, with a control that passes at an
occupancy inside the window. The six records above are the fixture - this is not a hypothetical
input.

## What this bead is NOT

**Separate from basicly-tcmy.34.** Three quantities exist, not two: the scope proxy
(`forecast_tokens`, 18780 to 66780 across these records), final window occupancy (`context_tokens`,
80211 to 223221) and whole-lane spend (`tokens`, 2393339 to 23963089). tcmy.34's 269x is the proxy
against *spend*. This bead is the declared window against *measured occupancy*.

**The band is a second-order question and is deliberately left out.** `decompose.py:792` states that
`working_set_max` is a context-window ceiling, so `DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX = 132000` and
`ceiling_tokens` are the same quantity and should not disagree. Against a corrected 600000 trigger
they no longer contradict outright, but the proxy still runs 3.16x to 7.21x low against measured
occupancy, so a lane admitted at 132000 lands near 495000 at the median ratio and near 950000 at the
worst - over the corrected trigger at the tail. `config.py:455-466` records that 132000 was derived
by re-reading the tree and re-applying the estimator to its own output, which
`run_record.py:164-171` explains was unavoidable before `context_tokens` existed. That field now has
seven samples, so the derivation can be replaced by a measurement - but only after the window is
right, because calibrating a band against a trigger that is itself wrong by 5x fits the error.
**File that as the follow-on; do not widen this bead into it.**

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_runner.py`

payload.close_reason: wontfix: NO-GO on the land-after-ship redesign. CI-cost driver already solved by flp; c9e5 and 4psl removed loop friction; residual governance+efficiency gains do not justify a high-risk reorder of phase-derivation/fan-in/rework/concurrency on a just-stabilized loop (P3). payload.description:
Follow-up design track from basicly-flp. Today the loop lands a worktree at the build->verify transition, BEFORE the verify phase gate and the human ship checkpoint, and closes the bead in a separate post-ship tracker-only commit; merge_worktree also verifies twice (in the worktree post-rebase, then again on base via _record_verify, an identical tree). Proposed redesign: reorder to build -> verify (gate recorded from the worktree run) -> ship checkpoint -> land+close in one step, where the merge uses git merge --no-ff --no-commit, then closes the bead, flushes, stages .beads/issues.jsonl, and commits - one tracker-carrying merge commit per track, nothing lands on main before gates and human approval, and the duplicate base re-verify disappears. Must be designed against: feature fan-in (children land through the queue when all closed - their self-landing order changes), rework semantics after a landing failure, multi-track concurrency (base working-tree jsonl carrying another track's uncommitted claim at merge time), and loop_state phase derivation (verified currently implies a bound worktree + green gates; landing evidence moves). See the investigation and decision comments on basicly-flp.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A design comment (or architecture.md section update) covers phase reorder, fan-in, rework, concurrency, and phase-derivation impacts with a go/no-go recommendation; if go, implementation is decomposed into child beads. Full gate suite passes for anything landed.
payload.title: Design: land after ship approval and fold the bead close into the merge commit

payload.text: Scoped down by basicly-c9e5 (br redirect worktrees + engine-owned tracker commits): once c9e5 ships, the residual value here is governance only - landing before ship approval, and folding the close into the merge commit saves one CI-free engine commit. Re-evaluate go/no-go after c9e5.

DESIGN GO/NO-GO: NO-GO (wontfix). Analysis of the proposed reorder (build -> verify[gate from worktree run] -> ship checkpoint -> land+close in one --no-ff --no-commit merge commit) against the required impact areas:

- Driver reassessment: the original motivation (pointless CI builds from tracker commits) was already solved by flp via paths-ignore .beads/** on the workflows + consumer template. c9e5 then made worktrees share the tracker via br redirect (no diverging issues.jsonl copy), and 4psl made the landing rebase conflict-free when work is committed. The loop is now stable and frictionless, so only two residual benefits remain: (1) governance - today code lands on main at build->verify, BEFORE the human ship checkpoint, so ship approval gates only teardown/close, not the merge; (2) efficiency - one fewer commit (fold close into the merge) and dropping the duplicate verify (worktree pre-merge check + base post-merge recorded run on an identical tree).

- Phase reorder impact: moving the merge to after the ship checkpoint inverts the state machine. loop_state currently derives 'verified' from a bound worktree + green required gate + a landed branch; landing evidence would move, so phase derivation and the _worktree_landed backstop (ship refuses an unlanded branch) both need reworking.
- Feature fan-in impact: children currently land through the serial merge queue at the parent build phase, and a child driven through its own loop self-lands at ITS ship. Landing the parent after ship changes when children land relative to parent approval - fan-in ordering and the 'already self-landed' accounting must be redesigned.
- Rework impact: a landing that fails AFTER a human has approved ship is a new failure mode (today landing precedes approval, so a landing failure reworks before any human gate). Recovery semantics post-approval are undefined.
- Concurrency impact: the --no-commit merge + stage .beads/issues.jsonl + commit would sweep any other in-flight track's uncommitted tracker claim sitting in the base working tree at merge time - a cross-track contamination risk the current commit_tracker_state path avoids.

- Decision: NO-GO. The CI-cost driver is solved; c9e5+4psl removed the friction; the residual wins are modest governance + efficiency on a P3, against a high-risk reorder spanning phase-derivation, fan-in, rework, and concurrency, on a loop that was just stabilized. Rejected alternative kept as-is. The one reason to revisit: if 'nothing lands on main before human ship approval' becomes a hard governance requirement (e.g. a production-agent/Foundry principle), reopen and decompose - but note deterministic verify gates already pass before landing, so the ship checkpoint is effectively a final formality today.

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-07 by exercising `basicly-u6jq.2` on live work, hours after it landed. The
delegated decompose proposer is dispatched, produces a plan, and the plan is then refused or
lands a child that cannot be built - **because the prompt does not carry rules the
`harness-loop` skill states**. Two instances, same root cause.

Both are cheap to fix and both convert a delegated phase back into a human stop, which is the
exact thing the dark factory exists to remove.

## Steps to Reproduce

### Instance 1 - `shared` prose contradicts the output contract

1. Take a bead whose scope includes a shared anchor (a README or an architecture status
   table). `basicly-imnu.2` is one.
2. Run `basicly loop run basicly-imnu.2 --work-type feature --root basicly-imnu.2`.

Observed:

```
[blocked] classify -> classify: decompose needs an agent-proposed child plan; the proposed
child plan failed the plan schema: children[0] 'shared' entry
'docs/architecture/architecture.md' is not in that child's 'scope'; declare the path in
'scope' too, so the recorded scope stays the whole truth (needs input: children)
```

Expected: the plan validates, or the proposer is told the rule it must satisfy.

The cause is a contradiction inside one prompt in `src/basicly/loop.py`, about seven lines
apart. The prose:

> list under 'shared' any literal path the child touches **but does not own**

The output contract immediately below it:

> `"shared": ["<literal path already in scope>", ...]`

These say opposite things. A path a child "does not own" is precisely a path not in its
`scope`, and the validator enforces the second reading - `shared` must be a subset of
`scope`. A proposer that follows the prose, which is stated first and in natural language,
is refused every time.

`.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml` has it right: "also list in `shared` any
literal path **from its `scope`** the child only appends its own entry to". The prompt's
prose diverged from the skill it implements.

### Instance 2 - the proposer types a leaf-shaped child as `feature`

1. Run the same proposer against `basicly-3ifz`.
2. It produced `basicly-3ifz.1` - a good plan, five well-formed acceptance criteria, correct
   scope - typed **`feature`**.

Observed: `basicly-3ifz.1` is a single coherent change (one new module, one CLI subcommand,
two test files) and a `feature` blocks at decompose demanding a child plan of its own,
provisioning no worktree. It had to be retyped by hand to `task` before it could be built.

Expected: the proposer classifies a child by shape.

The cause is that the prompt states the enum, `"type": "<bug|chore|task|feature>"`, and gives
no rule for choosing. The skill does give the rule: "classify by shape, not by ambition: one
coherent change is a `task`, and only work that genuinely fans out into separately landable
children is a `feature`. A `feature` blocks at decompose demanding a child plan and
provisions no worktree, so a leaf-shaped bead filed as one stalls before any code is
written."

## Cost

Measured this session: two proposer dispatches at 64,789 and 69,082 tokens. Cheap per
occurrence, but instance 1 blocks the lane outright and instance 2 lands a child that stalls
on its first dispatch. A shared anchor is the common case for a fan-out, not the rare one.

## Fix

Carry both rules into the prompt from the skill that already states them. For instance 1
correct the prose - it is the wrong half. **Do not relax the validator**, which is right for
the reason its own message gives: the recorded scope has to stay the whole truth, and a
`shared` path outside `scope` is a file the child writes without declaring.

Add a regression test that the prompt and the plan validator agree on the subset rule. A
contradiction between two strings in one prompt is caught by no existing gate, which is why
this reached live work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the decompose proposer prompt when it is generated then it states the shared-is-a-subset-of-scope rule exactly once and in one direction, carries the classify-by-shape rule for a child type, and a test fails if the prompt and the plan validator disagree on either rule

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

payload.description:
The release workflow runs `uv build` then uploads `files: dist/*` (.github/workflows/release.yml:156). `uv build` writes a 1-byte `dist/.gitignore` (contents `*`) into the output dir, and the wildcard glob sweeps it onto the GitHub release page as a stray attachment alongside the real wheel and sdist.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Tag a release (push a `v*` tag) so the release job runs.
2. Open the published release and look at the Assets list.
3. A 1-byte `.gitignore` appears as an asset next to `basicly-<v>-py3-none-any.whl` and `basicly-<v>.tar.gz`.

Reproduced locally: `uv build --out-dir <dir>` emits a `.gitignore` (1 byte, contents `*`) beside the wheel and tarball.

## Root Cause
`files: dist/*` matches every file uv drops in `dist/`, including its scratch `.gitignore`, so the glob is too broad.
payload.title: release uploads a stray gitignore asset from the build output dir

payload.description:
VS Code loads both .claude/rules/*.md and .github/instructions/*.instructions.md with no dedup — it name-dedupes only skills (user-shared findings from a separate research session, 2026-07-16; metadata-alignment hypotheses were tested and disproved there). Path-scoped guidance therefore double-loads in VS Code for every consumer. That session adopted single-source emission (scoped rules to .claude/rules only, .github/instructions twins swept, a verifier failing if they reappear) — a basicly install refresh in a repo with that policy would regress it, so this must land before the next consumer refresh.

Change the default projection so scoped rules emit to .claude/rules/ only:
- copilot target keeps .github/copilot-instructions.md (root trio unchanged — each file has a distinct native reader)
- skills stay dual-emitted (.claude/skills + .agents/skills): Claude reads only the former, Codex only the latter, and VS Code safely name-dedupes them
- install/uninstall sweep previously manifest-tracked .github/instructions/*.instructions.md files in consumers
- trade-off, accepted: github.com-side Copilot (PR code review, cloud agent) loses path-scoped rules and keeps only the root copilot-instructions.md

## Acceptance Criteria
- basicly build/install no longer emits .github/instructions/*.instructions.md; basicly's own two files (python-style, test-discipline) are swept from .github/instructions/
- .github/copilot-instructions.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and .claude/rules/*.md output is unchanged
- skills remain dual-emitted to .claude/skills and .agents/skills
- a consumer re-running basicly install has its stale .github/instructions projections removed (manifest-driven)
- docs/architecture.md targets section records the single-source policy and the github.com trade-off
- tests cover the removed target and the stale-file sweep
payload.title: single-source scoped rules: stop emitting .github/instructions by default

## Context

Recurring shape, third occurrence recorded (memory 2026-08-2x, basicly-85cadb, 2026-08-28 basicly-6mfhjp): a landing runs `verify full`, which runs tests whose population is the whole committed ledger, so a marker written by any other lane's dispatch can refuse this lane's landing. The lane is then charged a rework and briefed a repair for a defect that is not in its diff and cannot be fixed from its worktree. `.scripts/check_release_notes.py` already solved the same shape for its gate with `landing(repo, record_id)`, judged against the lane rather than the tree (basicly-qorx).

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a landing's verify run fails a check or test whose subject is a tracker record other than the landing lane, the landing SHALL report the failure as a base finding naming that record, SHALL not charge the lane a rework, and SHALL not brief a repair in the lane's worktree.
- WHEN the ledger-population tests run inside a landing, THEY SHALL evaluate the landing lane's own records and the base's state separately, so the verdict says which side owes the fix.
- WHEN the failure belongs to the base, the supervisor SHALL hold every landing in the pass with the base finding as the reason, and route one repair to the base rather than one per lane.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_merge_landing.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: a fixture landing whose only failure is another record's spend pair is routed as a base finding with rework unchanged.

payload.description:
## Context

Claude Code output styles modify the system prompt to set role, tone and default response
format. This repo had none, so every session ran the built-in Default style.

The owner's standing preference - answer first, brevity, structure over prose, disagree when
warranted, flag the claims most likely to be confidently wrong - existed only as a hand-pasted
chat prompt. A committed project output style makes it the default for everyone working in the
repo instead.

## Decisions

- **`keep-coding-instructions: true` is mandatory here.** A custom style *omits* Claude Code's
  built-in software-engineering instructions by default (verified against the vendor doc
  2026-08-06: "Custom output styles leave out Claude Code's built-in software engineering
  instructions, such as how to scope changes, write comments, and verify work, unless
  keep-coding-instructions is set to true"). In a repo whose whole subject is verification
  discipline, losing 'how to verify work' would be the worst possible regression.
- **Mermaid is excluded, tables and ASCII are not.** Claude Code renders markdown in a
  terminal, so a mermaid block shows as source. The style names the formats that actually
  render.
- **Length was the binding constraint.** The source chat prompt is ~600 words; the style is
  ~175. Every clause of the original was mapped before cutting, and the six that had been
  abstracted away were restored. Shorter is likelier to bind, and output styles get periodic
  adherence reminders that reinforce a short instruction set.
- **Phrased affirmatively.** Prohibitions cost context and read as noise; each rule states what
  to do.

## Why settings.json is safe to hand-edit

`.claude/settings.json` is committed but not projected: it is absent from
`.basicly/generated-manifest.json`, carries no generated marker, and `claude_settings.py`
merges only `permissions`, `hooks` and `worktree.bgIsolation` into it. Verified by running
`basicly permissions-build` and `basicly hooks-build` and confirming `outputStyle` survived
both.

## Scope

- `.claude/output-styles/tired-engineer.md`
- `.claude/settings.json`
payload.title: Ship a shared answer-first output style for Claude Code

payload.description:
## Context

Found by the lane-E cross-cutting survey 2026-08-14, with a syntax-tree probe over 202 classes and 695 functions.

`Ratchet`, `RatchetError`, `Module`, `Finding`, `load_ratchet`, `tracked_modules`, `waiver_reason`, `collect`, `report`, `main` and the scope-root tuple are each defined in all three of `check_module_size.py`, `check_comment_density.py` and `check_noqa_debt.py`.

The scope roots agree today at `module_size:80`, `noqa:77` and `density:42`. That agreement is luck. A fourth root added to one script silently unscopes the other two gates.

The composer divergence is the proof this triplication already produced a defect.

## Cost warning

Extracting code out of these scripts changes their own measurements. The three check scripts are not in the frozen list, and a move raises the remaining prose share of each. Measure the extracted unit's prose share against each origin before choosing the cut.

## Acceptance

- When the shared framework class is searched under the script directory, then exactly one definition exists.
- When each of the three gates runs, then its verdict on the current tree is unchanged and all three exit zero.
- When a scope root is added, then all three gates see it.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_module_size.py`
- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`
- `.scripts/check_noqa_debt.py`
- a new module under the script directory
- their tests

## Depends on

The delta route for the comment-density ratchet. Composition must be uniform before the loader is shared.

## Demonstration

All three scripts run and print three green lines identical to today's.

## Context

Owner retro 2026-08-23: a fresh context is right for review, architecture and analysis - independence is the point - but an implementer working the same feature re-derives the repo from zero every dispatch, 1-3M tokens before the first edit, measured on every lane today. The mechanism is already measured: --resume --fork-session gives ~10x cheaper warm starts, one-time penalty per working directory (plan row ejdm). What is missing is the policy: per-role inheritance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a dispatch role is implementer or repair on a feature with a seeded session, THE DISPATCH SHALL fork the seeded session instead of starting cold.
- WHEN the role is a reviewer, validator, decider or retrospector, THE DISPATCH SHALL stay cold, and the policy names why.
- WHEN no seed exists, THE FIRST DISPATCH SHALL create it.
- Demonstrated by: two consecutive implementer dispatches on one feature, the second's cache-read share and cost against today's cold baseline.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/roles.py`

## Context

The owner asks that the board be visible before development starts, because it is the human's view of open, in-progress and planned work. The board is engine code (`src/basicly/board_*.py`), not a kit: `.basicly/core/kit/` holds `tier` and `tracker` only, so a kit-only repository has no board to start. `basicly board serve` acquires no lock and writes no file, so nothing can tell whether one is running; there is no `[board]` port in `basicly.toml` and no VS Code task starts it. An always-on instruction telling every agent to start a server is wrong for a headless lane (no viewer, one server per lane) and violates the session-finish rule that no background process outlives the session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `basicly session start` runs and a board answers on the configured loopback port, IT SHALL print one line with the URL and the snapshot age; WHEN none answers, IT SHALL print the command that starts one; IT SHALL never start a server itself.
- WHEN `[board] port` is absent from `basicly.toml`, THE command SHALL use the documented default and say so.
- WHEN the repository has no owned tracker, THE line SHALL be absent.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_cli_session.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: with `uv run basicly board serve --port 8377` running, `uv run basicly session start` prints `board: http://127.0.0.1:8377 (snapshot 12 s old)`; after stopping it, the same command prints `board: not running - uv run basicly board serve`.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-02: "there is 1 in ship - we do not know why it is not drained." At the same moment the alarm band read `NOTHING IS WAITING - no checkpoint and no decision is pending`.

Measured. `/snapshot.json` `units[]` holds one record at phase `ship`: basicly-b2n2, "A stale database auto-flush silently deletes committed records", parent basicly-vkh0. `basicly loop status basicly-b2n2` reads `gates: advance ALLOWED, passed: verify, checkpoints: ship`. Its ship checkpoint was approved by a human on 2026-08-22T19:51:34Z after waiting 615,101 s. Nothing has run `basicly loop advance basicly-b2n2` since, so the record has sat one step from closed for 11 days. Its worktree binding names `harness/basicly-b2n2`, and neither that branch nor that worktree exists on disk; main carries `c07153a3 chore(beads): tidy the stale worktree reference`. The board's `asks` section is `[]` because it lists pending checkpoints and decisions only. A record whose next advance is allowed, that has no lane and no supervisor over its root, is the exact case a human must act on, and the board calls it nothing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8377/snapshot.json | jq '[.units[] | select(.phase=="ship")], .asks'`. Observed: one unit, `asks: []`.
2. `uv run basicly loop status basicly-b2n2`. Observed: `advance ALLOWED`.
3. Expected on the board: a row under the alarm band naming basicly-b2n2, its title, `ship - advance allowed`, the age since the last event (11 days), and the command the engine names as the next step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a unit's next advance is allowed and no lane and no supervisor holds its root, THE SNAPSHOT SHALL carry it as an ask of kind `advance`, with the record id, the phase, the age since its last event and the engine's remedy command.
- WHEN such an ask exists, THE ALARM BAND SHALL NOT read `NOTHING IS WAITING`; it SHALL count the ask and colour by the age, with the same thresholds the checkpoint asks use.
- WHEN the record advances or closes, THE ASK SHALL clear on the next fold.
- WHEN the snapshot lacks the field, THE TEMPLATE SHALL say so in the `not drawn` inventory, never default to zero.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_schema.py`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Reopened and re-prioritised 2026-07-29 after probing the live copilot CLI. The premise
recorded in `src/basicly/runner.py:153` is wrong and must be corrected with this work:
copilot does report token usage. The comment says its result event "carries premium-request
counts, not tokens", which is true of that one event and false as a generalisation.

Verified against `copilot -p ... --output-format json` plus the persisted session store:

- `result.usage` carries only `premiumRequests`, `totalApiDurationMs`, `sessionDurationMs`
  and `codeChanges` - no tokens. This is what the earlier probe saw.
- `session.usage_checkpoint.data` carries `totalNanoAiu` and `totalPremiumRequests`.
- `assistant.message.data` carries `model` and `outputTokens`.
- `model.call_start.data` carries `model` per call.
- `session.shutdown.data.modelMetrics.<modelId>` carries the whole thing, keyed by model:
  `requests{count,cost}`, `usage{inputTokens,outputTokens,cacheReadTokens,cacheWriteTokens,
  reasoningTokens}`, `totalNanoAiu`, and `tokenDetails`.

Observed on a one-word probe: inputTokens 24210, cacheWriteTokens 24208, outputTokens 4,
totalNanoAiu 6056400000 - that is 6.0564 AI credits.

The extraction wrinkle: `session.shutdown` is **not** emitted on stdout in headless `-p`
mode. It is persisted to the session store. So the reader is two-step - take
`result.sessionId` from the stream, then read that session's `events.jsonl`. The store path
is machine-local and must never be committed; it needs a config-overridable base rather than
a hardcoded home-relative path.

Because `modelMetrics` is already keyed by model id, this is the richest calibration carrier
of any adapter we have - it supplies the per-model token counts and a native cost figure that
basicly-jr0l.21 needs, for a family where nothing is recorded today.

Scope: `src/basicly/runner.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a completed copilot dispatch when its usage is read then the run record carries the
  per-model input output cache-read and cache-write token counts and the AI-credit cost taken
  from the session shutdown model metrics rather than the chars-over-four transcript estimate,
  and given a dispatch whose session store is absent or unreadable then the estimate fallback
  is used and recorded as an estimate rather than reported as measured, with tests
payload.design: Do not discover the state path - dictate it. RunnerSpec gains a state_env naming the variable that relocates the family's state root: COPILOT_HOME for copilot and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for claude, both verified present in the shipped binaries; unset for codex, which is not installed here and must not be guessed. run() already injects dispatch env (BR_MODEL at runner.py:568, GIT_AUTHOR and GIT_COMMITTER for the bot identity), so set state_env to a harness-owned directory under the gitignored .basicly/usage tree and read usage from a location known by construction. Verified 2026-07-29: with COPILOT_HOME pointed at a scratch dir the session landed in that dir's session-state and not in the real home, and the dispatch still exited 0 because copilot auth comes from the gh credential store rather than from COPILOT_HOME. This removes the platform path table entirely - no home-directory guessing across Windows, Linux, macOS and WSL, and no wslpath mapping for a Windows binary invoked from WSL - and it makes the path derive from the repo root so nothing machine-specific can reach a committed file. Side benefit: per-dispatch state dirs make concurrent lanes hermetic, which they are not today. Residual risks to handle in the work: a Windows binary reached from WSL needs a Windows-shaped value, which is the one real platform branch and belongs in table-driven test data rather than host-dependent logic per the platform-hermetic rule; a consumer whose auth does live in the copilot home breaks on relocation, so an empty state dir after a failed dispatch must fall back to the default home and record that it did; and a family with no known state_env falls through to usage-unmeasurable, which basicly-jr0l.35 governs.
payload.title: Copilot usage extraction: credits from session usage checkpoint

payload.text: User-supplied rate 2026-07-22 (unverified, AFAIK-grade): 1 copilot credit = 0.01 USD. That resolves the unit question: convert totalNanoAiu to USD as nanoAiu / 1e9 * 0.01 and keep RunRecord.cost USD-denominated - no unit-aware field needed. Verify the rate against GitHub billing docs (or 'copilot billing') before hardcoding; the probe example totalNanoAiu=6044400000 would be 6.0444 credits = 0.060444 USD.

Rate confirmed by official source: GitHub docs, usage-based billing for individuals (docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/billing/usage-based-billing-for-individuals) states 'This total is converted into AI credits (1 AI credit = 0.01 USD)'. Safe to hardcode the nanoAiu/1e9*0.01 conversion; cite this page in the code comment.

[harness-info] Promoted to the release path 2026-07-29. The consequence is not only bad telemetry: policy.session_spend_tokens (the grant meter) sums these recorded token values, so on copilot the autonomy grant's spend ceiling meters a chars-over-four estimate taken over captured output only. Measured 1378 estimated against 24210 real input tokens on a live probe, 17.6 times under with json output and about 24000 times under with text output. Same failure class as basicly-jr0l.22 - a ceiling that cannot fire - reached by a different route. The general case is basicly-jr0l.35.

[harness-info] Codex state root confirmed 2026-07-29 as CODEX_HOME (67 references in codex-cli 0.146.0), plus CODEX_SQLITE_HOME. Important difference from copilot: auth.json lives *inside* the codex home, so pointing CODEX_HOME at an empty directory would break auth - the residual risk flagged on this bead is real for codex specifically. Either seed the harness-owned home with the auth file or relocate only the sqlite state via CODEX_SQLITE_HOME, leaving CODEX_HOME alone. Copilot is unaffected because its auth comes from the gh credential store.

payload.description:
## Context

The measurement basicly-tjhjmk was opened for, taken 2026-08-27 on this tree with
`.basicly/usage/scratch/baseline.py` (each declared check run exactly as `verify._run`
runs it) and confirmed by a real landing through the new `merge._Landing` instrument.

**A landing runs the full verify suite twice.**

1. `merge._verify_for_landing` runs `verify.run_verify(worktree_path, "full")` after the
   rebase — 132.4s.
2. `loop._record_verify` (`src/basicly/loop.py:2097`) runs `verify.run_verify(repo_root,
   "full")` again in the base checkout *after* the merge has already happened — 132.4s.

That is ~265s of a landing the owner retro clocked at 3-8 minutes. Inside one full run:

| check | seconds | share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pytest | 84.35 | 64% |
| pyright-linux | 10.93 | 8% |
| pyright-darwin | 10.72 | 8% |
| pyright-windows | 10.59 | 8% |
| the other 34 checks | 15.8 | 12% |

`fast` (34 checks, unscoped) is 26.4s, of which `pyright` is 11.0s. The landing also pays
that chain twice more, in the tracker-sync commit and in the merge commit, scoped to the
staged diff — that scoped figure is **not** measured here, and the new per-stage record
answers it on the next real landing (`tracker-commit` and `merge` stages).

## The cut

The second full run is the candidate: it re-runs, in base, the suite that just passed in
the worktree on the same content. `_record_verify`'s job is to *record the gate*, and it
runs a suite to have something to record. Whether the first run's `VerifyReport` can be
carried to the gate record instead is the question — the trees are not identical (the
merge commit exists in base), so this needs an argument, not an assumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the cut lands, THE RECORD SHALL carry the before/after from
  `.basicly/usage/landing-timings.json`, measured over real landings, not estimated.
- WHEN the second full run is removed or narrowed, THE VERIFY GATE SHALL still be recorded
  against evidence from a tree that includes the merge commit, or the record shall state
  why that is not needed.
- Demonstrated by: two landings' recorded breakdowns, before and after, with the verify
  stage total named in each.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

## Trigger

When a landing repeats full verification on an unchanged source input set, I want proven deterministic results carried into the gate, so I can shorten landing time without accepting stale evidence.

## Context

Existing record basicly-tjhjmk measured two full executions. Current child.4 landing ran all three Pyright platform checks twice; full suites passed7020 tests each, with first landing verify178.787s. The existing landing timer excludes the second verification. Existing raw inputs selectors only control staged selection and do not prove complete reusable inputs. Child.4 repaired recurring gate verdicts before this work.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_receipt.py`
- `src/basicly/pyright_inputs.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_artifact.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_verify_receipt.py`
- `tests/test_pyright_inputs.py`
- `tests/test_verify_artifact.py`
- `tests/test_merge_timing.py`
- `tests/test_loop_lane.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `docs/how-to/wire-up-the-verify-gate.md`
- `changelog.d/basicly-2tfuwv.changed.md`

## Design

Carry the actual successful VerifyReport from merge to gate recording. Reuse requires an explicit reviewed recipe and matching check argv, mode, complete input inventory and content, configuration, platform, interpreter, tool/runtime and execution environment. Capture before and after execution; changed or unreadable inputs invalidate reuse. Only passed executed observations qualify. Missing, failed, skipped, stale, unsupported or absent receipts execute the checks normally.

First enable the three existing full Pyright platform checks with a version-bounded recipe for installed1.1.411. Cover source additions, removals, renames, module shadowing, config/search paths, type stubs, dependencies, runtime and environment. Bind equivalent workspace paths explicitly; unsupported external paths, configuration or runtime shapes fall back to fresh execution. Preserve dotenv denials. Do not infer reusable inputs from the old staged selectors or dependency-output filenames alone.

All other checks, including pytest and Git/ledger-sensitive checks, remain fresh until their complete contracts exist. This narrows the duplicate full pass; it does not complete the parent mixed-tech optimization goal. No persistent cross-run cache, affected selection, new dependencies or mandatory build system in this unit. Ordinary verify and Git hooks retain fresh execution; same-landing reuse stays inside the engine.

Record executed versus reused results and refusal reasons with source provenance. Measure post-merge verification and combined verification separately from existing merge timing. Cover leaf, queued-child, already-landed and manual paths: missing proof always runs normally.

## Measurement

Use retained real child.3/child.4 before evidence and actual candidate landings; prove compiler invocation counts independently of timing. Target elimination of the three redundant platform compiler processes (previously about30s combined) with at most1s warm fingerprint overhead on this repository. Report measured before/after values and conditions, including fallback/cold cases; do not claim improvement from skipped tests or estimates. The 50k/200k/1M mixed-stack scaling experiment remains on basicly-c25o52c.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_verify_receipt.py tests/test_pyright_inputs.py tests/test_verify_artifact.py tests/test_merge_timing.py tests/test_loop_lane.py tests/test_config.py -q`

Build the release wheel and run the real loop as a consumer in isolated repositories. An unchanged supported landing reuses only proven compiler results; a changed/unsupported input reruns them and a real compiler failure blocks advancement. Upgrade from released0.24.1 without altering consumer checks.

import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

artifacts = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
root = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve() if len(sys.argv) > 1 else artifacts
root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
runtime = root / "package-env"
old = Path('<redacted:posix-absolute-path>')
new = artifacts / 'reviewed-launcher-dist/basicly-0.24.1-py3-none-any.whl'
assert hashlib.sha256(old.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == '3f4de59aa5aab24c581e9818749d25ede01a53dd2282b8737b58476e489aeaad'
env = os.environ.copy()
env.pop('PYTHONPATH', None)
env.update(UV_OFFLINE='1', UV_NO_SYNC='1', UV_CACHE_DIR='<redacted:posix-absolute-path>', UV_FIND_LINKS='<redacted:posix-absolute-path>', UV_LINK_MODE='copy', AI_AGENT='codex')
transcript = root / 'package-consumer.log'

def call(label, argv, cwd=root):
    result = subprocess.run([str(arg) for arg in argv], cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
    with transcript.open('a') as stream:
        stream.write(label + '\n' + result.stdout + result.stderr + '\nexit=' + str(result.returncode) + '\n')
    assert result.returncode == 0, (label, result.stdout[-2000:], result.stderr[-3000:])
    print(label, 'PASS', flush=True)
    return result.stdout

assert not runtime.exists()
call('create isolated package runtime', ['uv', 'venv', '--python', sys.executable, runtime])
python = runtime / 'bin/python'
engine = runtime / 'bin/basicly'
env['PATH'] = str(runtime / 'bin') + os.pathsep + env['PATH']
env['VIRTUAL_ENV'] = str(runtime)
call('install actual released engine offline', ['uv', 'pip', 'install', '--offline', '--python', python, old, 'pyright==1.1.411'])
call('warm real compiler launcher', [runtime / 'bin/pyright', '--version'])

config = '\n'.join(
    f'[[verify.checks]]\nname="types-{target}"\ncommand=["pyright","--pythonplatform","{target}"]\nmodes=["full"]\n'
    for target in ['Linux', 'Darwin', 'Windows']
)
config += '[[verify.checks]]\nname="tests"\ncommand=["python","-c","print(123)"]\nmodes=["full"]\n'

def prepare(name):
    repo = root / name
    repo.mkdir()
    call(name + ' init', ['git', 'init', '--quiet', '--initial-branch=main', repo])
    for key, value in [('user.name','Consumer Probe'), ('user.email','consumer@example.invalid'), ('core.hooksPath','.githooks')]:
        call(name + ' config ' + key, ['git','config',key,value], repo)
    (repo / 'src').mkdir()
    (repo / 'src/demo.py').write_text('value: int = 1\n')
    (repo / 'pyproject.toml').write_text('[project]\nname="receipt-consumer"\nversion="0.1.0"\nrequires-python=">=3.14"\ndependencies=[]\n[tool.pyright]\nvenvPath="."\nvenv=".venv"\ninclude=["src"]\nextraPaths=["src", "."]\n')
    (repo / 'basicly.toml').write_text(config)
    hooks = repo / '.githooks'
    hooks.mkdir()
    hook = hooks / 'pre-commit'
    hook.write_text('#!<redacted:posix-absolute-path>\nprintf "foreign\\n" >> "$(git rev-parse --git-path foreign-count)"\n')
    hook.chmod(0o755)
    call(name + ' analysis environment', ['uv','sync','--offline'], repo)
    call(name + ' harness install', [engine,'install'], repo)
    assert (repo / '.basicly/bin/lefthook').is_file()
    call(name + ' offline binary version', [repo / '.basicly/bin/lefthook','version'], repo)
    return repo

upgrade = prepare('upgrade-consumer')
before_config = (upgrade / 'basicly.toml').read_bytes()
before_lefthook = (upgrade / 'lefthook.yml').read_bytes()
baseline = '''
from pathlib import Path
import json
from basicly import verify
root=Path.cwd(); original=verify._spawn;calls=[]
def counted(command,*args,**kwargs):
 calls.append(command[0]);return original(command,*args,**kwargs)
verify._spawn=counted
first=verify.run_verify(root,'full');second=verify.run_verify(root,'full')
assert first.passed and second.passed
assert calls.count('pyright')==6 and calls.count('python')==2,calls
print(json.dumps({'compiler_invocations':calls.count('pyright'),'tests':calls.count('python')}))
'''
call('released baseline real six compiler invocations', [python,'-c',baseline], upgrade)
call('upgrade isolated package engine offline', ['uv','pip','install','--offline','--reinstall-package','basicly','--python',python,new])
call('upgrade harness from actual release', [engine,'install'], upgrade)
assert (upgrade / 'basicly.toml').read_bytes()==before_config
assert (upgrade / 'lefthook.yml').read_bytes()==before_lefthook
fresh=prepare('fresh-consumer')
probe='''
from pathlib import Path
import json
from basicly import verify
root=Path.cwd(); original=verify._spawn;calls=[]
def counted(command,*args,**kwargs):
 calls.append(command[0]);return original(command,*args,**kwargs)
verify._spawn=counted
origin=verify.run_verify(root,'full',capture_receipts=True)
assert origin.passed and len(origin.receipts)==3,origin
landed=verify.run_verify(root,'full',reuse=origin)
assert landed.passed and sum(bool(r.reused_from) for r in landed.results)==3,landed
assert calls.count('pyright')==3 and calls.count('python')==2,calls
(root/'src/added.py').write_text('broken: int = "not an int"\\n')
changed=verify.run_verify(root,'full',reuse=origin)
assert not changed.passed and calls.count('pyright')==6
assert all(not r.reused_from for r in changed.results)
print(json.dumps({'unchanged_compilers':3,'changed_compilers':3,'fresh_tests':calls.count('python'),'changed_failures':list(changed.failures),'source_duration_s':origin.duration_s,'reuse_duration_s':landed.duration_s}))
'''
for repo in (upgrade,fresh):
    call(repo.name + ' ordinary verify stays fresh', [python,'-c',baseline], repo)
    current=(repo/'basicly.toml').read_text()
    assert current.count('modes=["full"]')==4
    (repo/'basicly.toml').write_text(current.replace('modes=["full"]','modes=["full"]\nreuse="pyright"',3))
    call(repo.name + ' packaged receipt and failure probes', [python,'-c',probe], repo)
    assert call(repo.name + ' hooks path preserved',['git','config','core.hooksPath'],repo).strip()=='.githooks'
result={'result':'PASS','release_sha256':hashlib.sha256(old.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'candidate_sha256':hashlib.sha256(new.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'consumer_loop':'not yet exercised: actual task landing remains required','fresh_install':True,'upgrade_ownership':True,'offline_binary':True}
(root/'package-consumer-result.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
print(json.dumps(result),flush=True)

import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import statistics
import sys
import tempfile
import zipfile

from basicly import verify
from basicly.config import VerifyConfig, load_verify_config

root = Path.cwd()
output = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='basicly-final-merged-benchmark-'))
print(output, flush=True)
wheel = Path('<redacted:posix-absolute-path>')
modules = ['config', 'verify', 'verify_receipt', 'pyright_inputs', 'verify_artifact', 'merge', 'loop']
with zipfile.ZipFile(wheel) as archive:
    for name in modules:
        assert archive.read(f'basicly/{name}.py') == (root / f'src/basicly/{name}.py').read_bytes()
artifact = root / '.basicly/usage/verify-run.json'
original = artifact.read_bytes()
(output / 'original-verify-run.json').write_bytes(original)
calls = []

def observe(event, args):
    if event == 'subprocess.Popen' and Path(os.fsdecode(args[0])).name == 'pyright':
        calls.append({'argv': args[1], 'cwd': str(args[2])})

sys.addaudithook(observe)
try:
    config = VerifyConfig(tuple(check for check in load_verify_config(root).checks if check.reuse))
    assert len(config.checks) == 3
    source = verify.run_verify(root, 'full', config, capture_receipts=True)
    assert source.passed and len(source.receipts) == 3
    samples = []
    for _ in range(30):
        report = verify.run_verify(root, 'full', config, reuse=source)
        assert report.passed and sum(bool(result.reused_from) for result in report.results) == 3
        samples.append(report.duration_s)
    assert len(calls) == 3
    result = {
        'wheel_sha256': hashlib.sha256(wheel.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        'merged_modules_equal_wheel': modules,
        'source_duration_s': source.duration_s,
        'source_run_id': source.run_id,
        'samples_s': samples,
        'median_s': statistics.median(samples),
        'p95_nearest_rank_s': sorted(samples)[28],
        'compiler_processes': calls,
        'warm_reuse_runs': 30,
        'original_artifact_sha256': hashlib.sha256(original).hexdigest(),
        'limitation': 'Compiler-only same-checkout measurement. Not a full landing, cold machine, mixed-stack or size-scaling claim.',
    }
    (output / 'result.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)
finally:
    artifact.write_bytes(original)
    assert artifact.read_bytes() == original
    print('Original verification artifact restored byte-for-byte.', flush=True)

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-r4jm` gave seven of the eight named artifacts a schema. `solution-design` is the
exception, and deliberately so rather than by omission.

D17 (`factory-loop.md:95`) decides it is **markdown with six machine-checked sections**, not a
JSON payload: 'Structured markdown is the only shape that is both readable and checkable - JSON is
unreadable and prose is unactionable.' Every other handoff artifact is a JSON payload validated by
`handoff.record` against a `<kind>.schema.json` and persisted as a compact `[harness-artifact]`
marker. Those are two different mechanisms.

So the question is not 'write the missing schema'. It is whether `solution-design` belongs to the
handoff family at all, and if it does, what validates it - a section checker like the DoR gate
already uses, or a JSON schema over a payload derived from the sections.

Also found while correcting the table: `factory-loop.md:139` still says 'the five
`solution-design` sections' while D17 was amended to six on 2026-08-08. One of the two is wrong.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Read `factory-loop.md` section 8's artifact table: eight artifacts named.
- `ls .basicly/core/schemas/`: seven of the eight have a schema; `solution-design` has none.
- Read D17: it specifies markdown sections, which `handoff.record` cannot validate.

## Scope

- `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md`
- `src/basicly/handoff.py`

## Context

DeepSeek research 2026-08-17 §11.3 (architecture D-43), the one rule adopted beyond the token-cost declaration: the reference harness validates its exemption table against the scanned population - an entry naming a package that no longer exists fails, an entry with a blank justification fails, and variant spellings are rejected rather than presence checked. In this repository .scripts/check_waivers.py does this for the size waivers. The other exemption tables - [tool.noqa_debt], [tool.comment_density.frozen], [tool.module_size.frozen], [tool.spend_accuracy.frozen], [tool.docs_citations.unverifiable], the retired-vocabulary allowance, the test-naming exemptions - have not been audited for the same property, and architecture §32.1 records the matching defect in our own words: a gate written as prose is not a gate. Source at commit 78962968: docs/research/2026-08-17-deepseek-harness.md §11.3 and §12.8.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the audit runs, IT SHALL list every exemption table in pyproject.toml and basicly.toml and state for each whether an entry naming a member absent from its population is refused.
- WHEN a table admits an entry naming an absent member, A CHECK SHALL be added or the table's own gate extended so that it refuses, with a test that plants such an entry.

## Scope

- .scripts/check_*.py
- pyproject.toml
- tests/**
- changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md

## Context

Attempt 4 of the unattended-run proof failed on `docs/design/tier-injection-kit.md`
§7 'Open', which names `basicly-e3z6` and `basicly-5gn2` as bullets. Both lanes ran
concurrently, each deleted its own bullet, and the two edits hit one anchor — so the
second lane bounced, burned both rework attempts replaying the same rebase, and
escalated to a human.

The list is the tracker's content duplicated in prose. The implementation plan already
states the rule for the same problem one level up (§14): phase membership is a tracker
label and the plan says 'Query it rather than reading a list here', with
`br list --label phase-2`. A design document's open-items list is the same duplication
and creates the same collision.

## The fix

A design document says what the design **is**. What is still open about it is a tracker
query. Replace each hand-maintained bead-id list with the query that answers it —
a label per design area, so `br list --label kit` replaces §7 — and delete the lists.

Two properties follow: the list cannot go stale (it is generated on demand), and two
lanes closing two items in the same design area stop colliding, because neither edits
the document at all.

## Sweep, do not spot-fix

Find every such list rather than only the one that failed: grep the design and
architecture documents for bead-id references that function as status rather than as
citation. A citation of *why* a decision was made is history and stays; a list of what
remains open is state and goes.

## Scope

- `docs/design/tier-injection-kit.md`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`

Narrowed 2026-08-06 from the original five-file list after the sweep recorded in this bead's
comments. `factory-design.md`, `agent-roster-design.md` and `architecture.md` were checked and
carry citations only, so they are deliberately **out** of scope rather than unexamined. The label
minting the replacement query depends on is a `br` action, not a file.
payload.title: A design document must not carry a list of bead ids the tracker already owns

payload.text:
Swept 2026-08-06 at d58e8e2, before dispatching. Method: extract every `basicly-xxxx` token from
every file under `docs/`, **validate each against the 616 ids in `.beads/issues.jsonl`**, then group
by nearest heading. Validating against the tracker matters - a bare regex also matches
`.basicly-local/`, `basicly permissions-build` and the `basicly-fix-the-thing` example in
work-tracker R5, and a sweep that trusts the regex edits prose that references no bead at all.

Result: **233 real bead references across 14 documents.** Almost all are citations and stay. Two
are the defect.

## Confirmed targets (2, not the 5 files this bead's Scope listed)

1. **`docs/design/tier-injection-kit.md` §7 "Open"** (L189-195) - the instance that failed attempt
   4. A two-line section whose entire content is one bead id as status.
2. **`docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` §14 "Phase labels to epics"** (L603-615) - and this one is
   self-contradicting, which is the sharper finding. Two lines above the table it says *"Query it
   rather than reading a list here"* and prints `br list --label phase-2`. Then it prints a
   15-id table.

   **But the table is not uniformly wrong, so do not delete it.** Phase -> epic is one stable root
   per phase and is the *index into* the tracker, not a duplicate of its contents. What goes is the
   inline **status** in the Release column: ``(`u6jq.1` is all that remains)``, ``(`agzx.1` done)``,
   ``(`m4zv.14` in `v0.7.0`)``. That is the state that rots, and it is what two lanes closing two
   items in one phase would both edit.

## Explicit exclusions - a sweep that takes these is destructive

- **`docs/archive/**` - 45 references, do not touch.** Its own banner: *"Archived - spike complete
  (kept for design provenance) ... nothing here is maintained, and a claim in it is evidence of
  what was true in 2026-07 rather than of current behaviour."* Its dimension numbering is cited by
  `src/basicly/permissions.py` and `src/basicly/rubrics.py`. Archive is history by declaration,
  which is exactly the category this bead says stays.
- **`docs/design/work-tracker.md` §2.1, R1-R9** - each id is the citation for a paid-for
  dependency defect, and R9 is held by a completeness test
  (`test_r9_a_publish_that_would_shrink_the_export_is_refused_not_silent`). Deleting these deletes
  the provenance of a gated register.
- **`docs/design/factory-design.md` §3 components 10-11, §6 configuration defaults, §8** -
  citations: which pre-existing bead a component absorbs, and why a default has the value it has.
- **`docs/design/agent-roster-design.md` §8** - citations of which bead builds a mechanism this
  design depends on (`kjc5.16` confinement, `kjc5.4` decision queue).
- **`docs/architecture/architecture.md` §11 and §15** - checked and neither qualifies. §11 states
  outright *"None is tracked as an open issue"*; §15 keys rows on capability and design document,
  carrying no bead ids.
- **`docs/design/tier-injection-kit.md` §1** - the `Bead` table row identifies which bead each
  *approach* is, which is identification, not status.

## Blocking prerequisite: the replacement query returns nothing today

This bead's fix says *"a label per design area, so `br list --label kit` replaces §7"*. **That
label vocabulary does not exist.** The only labels in the tracker are `phase-0`..`phase-7`,
`phase-meta`, `phase-multi`, `bookkeeping`, `owner-decision`, `zero-dep`. `basicly-a3yi` - the one
bead §7 names - carries `phase-1` and nothing else.

So replacing §7 with `br list --label kit` as written would point the document at an **empty
result**, and an empty query is indistinguishable from "nothing is open". That is strictly worse
than the stale list it replaces: the list was wrong and looked wrong, the query is wrong and looks
authoritative.

**Order the work accordingly:** mint the label on the beads that belong to the design area, run the
query and confirm it returns them, and only then delete the prose. A doc pointing at a query is
only honest once the query answers.
