Revision 4 of design version 8 (replaces revision 3, which stays in this record history). It adds the orchestrator decisions of 2026-11-12 for the round-3 breaks C1 to C7. A fresh verifier checks only those fixes; it gates S3.

### Work tracker, design version 8, revision 4 (family `git-budget`)

Base: design version 7 ("v7", record basicly-gtb19bg.60). Measured facts: verify/RESULTS.md. Every command is `basicly-tracker` (packages/basicly-tracker/pyproject.toml:13). Hosts: GitHub only in the core (OD6); the format names no host.

#### 0. Overview

1. One small registry repository lists projects and owns every prefix.
2. One vault repository per project holds the backlog; it is the unit of read access.
3. Each machine has one bare clone per vault, a writer id kept in its state folder, and a queue beside the clone.
4. A write appends to the queue; a share pushes one commit built on the fetched head.
5. Claim, take and unassign push at once (a plain push is the compare-and-swap); other events wait for a bulk slot.
6. Order is first-parent commit order; git stores it once; an export writes it into each line.
7. A clone never retracts a commit it has seen; a rewrite stops shares until `fsck --repair`.
8. Code never changes a status; hooks and an audit link the tracker to the code.
9. Every view prints the data age.
10. A vault ends only with a stop event that names its successor.

Bad news first.

- Five or more claims in one second can take over 10 s (measured: 9 of 13, maximum 26.5 s).
- Any writer with push rights can write lines in another writer's name until identity binding (OD2) exists. X3 is partly met.

#### 1. Decisions

##### 1.1 Owner answers of 2026-11-12 (binding)

Owner decisions are OD1 to OD6 here, apart from requirement ids D1 to D7.

- **OD1, N4.** Claims answered within 10 s at p99; other events within about 4 minutes (1.2 T at 13 machines is 234 s); every view shows the data age.
- **OD2, identity binding (X2) and OD3, erasure (X5)**: deferred.
- **OD4, forecast (V6)**: waits until M5 is cut over.
- **OD5**: the commit hook refuses a commit with no record id (section 5). **OD6**: GitHub only in the core. **Core first**: S2b, S3, S4, S2c, S5a, S7 (section 12).

What a reader sees under the deferred OD2: when a writer id pushes under a commit author it never used before, `fsck` prints `writer <id> (<name>) pushed commit <sha> as <new author>; first seen as <old author>`. That line shows in every view's warning block and in the portfolio until a person runs `fsck --ack-author <id> <author>`. The events still count.

##### 1.2 SPEC.md rules that a vault retires or changes

For a vault, FORMAT.md replaces these rules; after cutover the old ledger is only a `migrate` source.

| SPEC.md rule | In a vault |
| --- | --- |
| 4.0 shards, `merge=union`, `compact` | Retired: one segment set per writer. |
| 4.1 per-item `seq`; 14 "order independence" | Retired: first-parent commit order; imported `seq` stays in `payload.legacy_seq`. |
| 4.1 forks, `resolve`, `acknowledge-loss` | Retired: holder verdicts; `fsck --repair`. |
| 4.5 "no format version event" | Changed: every line carries `v`. |
| 4.6 `totals` | Retired: the fold computes them. |
| Fields `id`, `record`, `kind`, `actor`, `ts`, `payload` | Kept. Added: `v`, `project`, `writer`, `session`, `via`. |

#### 2. Data

##### 2.1 Layer map

| Layer | Contents | May import |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kit (pure) | format, commit-shape check, fold, holder verdicts, config fold, budget arithmetic | standard library; no network, subprocess or environment |
| Transport | `git_runner.py` (the only subprocess), clone, fetch, share, deadlines, code-history reader | kit |
| Adapters | CLI, commit hook, agent hooks, board, CI template | transport, kit |

Only adapters read the environment. Slice S2b makes `environ` a required argument of `holders.py:80`, `writers.py:23` and `events.py:759-779`. T-layers enforces this.

##### 2.2 Repositories

- **Registry**: one per tracker; it owns every prefix. Events: `registry-created`, `person`, `project-register`, `prefix-alias`, `project-archive`, `ended`.
- **Vault**: one per project. Both start with a genesis commit; `vault.toml` (own uid, kind, registry uid, project uid) is read from genesis only.
- **Configuration is events**: bounded `config` events set bulk constants, minimum version, stale times, statuses and fields (P5).
- **Code repository**: `.basicly/tracker.toml` (registry uid, project uid) and one README line with the registry URL (C2, C3).
- **Machine state folder** (mode 0700; `icacls` on Windows): `writer.id` (kept across reclones); per vault `clone/` (bare), `queue.jsonl`, `sessions.json`, `log/`. The registry URL (state folder, README line or `attach --registry <url>`) is accepted only when its genesis uid matches `tracker.toml`.

##### 2.3 Ids and sessions

- Registry, vault, project, writer and person ids: random 128-bit (P2, P4).
- Event id: writer id plus 128 random bits, fixed at queue time. `link`, `miss` and `claim-lost` ids are content hashes.
- Record id: `<prefix>-<root>.<n>` (SPEC.md 9.4). A rename adds an alias; the old prefix stays owned (P3).
- Holder: (writer id, session id). Session id, first match wins: (1) `--session <id>` minted by this clone; (2) `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; (3) `BASICLY_TRACKER_SESSION` from `session new`; (4) the machine's person session. Rule 4 is refused when an agent marker variable is set (assumed; P-session), so two agents never share a holder (D3).

##### 2.4 Files

Layout: `log/<writer-id>/<nnnnn>.jsonl`; the first line of a segment is the writer header. A new segment starts at 1.5 MB: files of 1.39 MB cost 640 B per event, files of 7.3 MB cost 3.3 KB (measured, normal repack, verify/storage).

An archive commit packs the open tails of writers idle for 90 days into `log/archive/<nnnnn>.jsonl`, byte for byte. At 1,000,000 events of 1.39 KB: 927 full segments, 50 live tails, 1 archive tail, about 978 files (arithmetic; T-storage decides).

##### 2.5 Event format and commit shapes

```text
{"v":1,"id":"…","ts":"2026-11-12T09:00:00Z","project":"…","record":"abc-k3x9.2",
 "kind":"claim","writer":"…","session":"…","via":"agent","actor":"<person id>","payload":{}}
```

- Every release reads every earlier `v` (L1). `ts` is UTC RFC 3339, evidence only (L6). `actor` is the responsible person (D4).
- Unknown kinds and fields are kept and skipped. A kind that changes holders or status carries `"fold":true`; an old tool meeting an unknown one refuses holder commands on that record and names the upgrade (A1).
- **Stop kind** (reserved in v1): `ended`, with `reason` (`moved`, `continued`, `rolled-back`), successor URL and uid. Every v1 tool refuses writes to a repository that holds a valid `ended`.

**One validity rule.** A clone reads the default branch in first-parent order and takes each line's bytes from the commit that added it. Each commit has one shape:

1. **Genesis**: no parent; adds exactly `vault.toml`, `FORMAT.md`, `reader.py`, `README.md`.
2. **Format**: one parent; changes only `FORMAT.md`, `reader.py` or `README.md`; carries no events.
3. **Batch**: one parent; only appends lines under `log/<w>/` for one writer `w`; a new segment starts with a header naming `w`; (2b) every event line's `writer` is `w`; no line is changed or removed.
4. **Archive**: one parent; moves whole files verbatim into `log/archive/`; the clone checks the bytes.

Any other commit is quarantined alone and reported. Nothing after a valid `ended` counts. Order is commit order, then line order; exports write it as `ord`. A git clone or an export is the portable form; files without history are readable but unordered.

**Fetch.** One fetch lock per clone serializes fetches. The bare clone fetches `+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`; the head is `refs/remotes/origin/main`. A failed fetch is retried once; then the command uses the last state and prints its age.

**Never retract.** The clone keeps local refs `refs/basicly/seen` and `refs/basicly/retracted/<n>` (never pushed, safe from `gc`). After every fetch, if the head's first-parent chain lacks the seen tip, the clone marks it retracted, refuses to share, and names `basicly-tracker fsck --repair`; otherwise it validates the new commits and moves `refs/basicly/seen` to the head. `reclone` copies both refs into the new clone.

**Repair.** `fsck --repair` re-queues every line on a retracted ref that is not valid on the head: own lines as they were, other writers' lines inside one `requeue` event that keeps their ids and changes no holder. A claim that no longer holds gets a `claim-lost` event, shown to its holder at the next hook and command. `fsck --accept-rewrite <head> --purge` drops retracted refs for a deliberate purge.

#### 3. Write, share and read

##### 3.1 Write

A command redacts secrets and absolute paths with a standard-library redactor that ships in the wheel (new in slice S3; X4) and runs on every write path, appends to `queue.jsonl` under `LedgerLock` with `fsync`, and prints `shared` or `queued (<n> events, oldest <age>); shares at your next tracker command or hook`. With `CI` or `BASICLY_TRACKER_EPHEMERAL` set, every write shares at once. Core agent hooks (slice S3): SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit fetch (3 s deadline, at most every 20 s) and run a due share; Stop and SessionEnd share the whole queue (SessionEnd assumed; P-session).

##### 3.2 Share

Under the share lock, plumbing only:

1. Fetch (section 2.5). If the head holds any valid `ended`, stop: keep the queue, and for `moved` or `continued` re-target it to the successor; `rolled-back` has no successor, so the command prints that the project rolled back and keeps the queue for `uninstall --export`.
2. Drop queued events whose ids are valid on the head.
3. Build the commit on the head with `hash-object`, a temporary index, `write-tree` and `commit-tree`; a crash leaves only unreferenced objects.
4. Push plainly. On refusal, go to step 1: an urgent share retries until the 30 s claim deadline; a bulk share retries at most 5 times.
5. On success, move `refs/basicly/seen`, then remove the shared events from the queue under `LedgerLock`.

A share sends its starting queue plus one more pass (v7 drain bound).

##### 3.3 Push budget

- **Urgent**: claim, take, unassign, project register. They push at once and carry the whole queue.
- **Bulk**: all others. They ride on an urgent push, or share at the first trigger after `T = max(60 s, M × 60 / 4)` times a random 0.8 to 1.2 (the simulated rule, sim.py:144-146). M is the number of writers with a commit in the last hour.
- **Triggers**: every command, every agent hook, the commit and pre-push hooks, the board every 30 s.
- **Bursts**: one clone per machine puts its sessions' claims into one push; nothing more is promised (S4 not met for 5 or more claims in one second).

##### 3.4 Claim protocol

`basicly-tracker claim <id>` has one 30 s deadline; each git call gets only the time that remains.

1. Validate the id and session (section 2.3). Missing: exit 1.
2. `git ls-remote`, at most 5 s. No answer: exit 5; nothing is queued.
3. Fetch and fold. Held by this session: exit 7. Held by another session: exit 3, with no push.
4. Append the claim to the queue and share. Another session on this machine may push it; that counts the same.
5. When the claim is valid on the head, fold. First claim: exit 0. Otherwise: exit 3.
6. Deadline: exit 4, "unsettled: do not start work; run basicly-tracker claim <id> --wait, or --cancel".

An unsettled claim is never held; the next command or core hook retries it. `claim <id> --cancel` takes the share lock, fetches, and drops the claim, or unassigns it if it landed. After 10 minutes it expires the same way.

Exit codes for every command, with the next command printed: 0 done; 1 refused by name, with the fix; 2 usage, `--help`; 3 held by another session, `claim <id> --take --reason "<text>"`; 4 unsettled, `--wait` or `--cancel`; 5 offline, `git ls-remote <url>` then retry; 6 internal error without traceback, the log path and `sync` (`doctor` from slice S10); 7 already held by this session.

##### 3.5 Holder changes

- `claim <id> --take --reason <text>` refuses a fresh claim unless `--force`. Without `--reason` it works only on a same-writer session idle for 30 minutes in `sessions.json`: resume after `/clear` (D2). Every take is logged; the old holder sees "taken by <name>: <reason>" at its next hook.
- `unassign <id> [--to <holder>]` is valid only from the holder (fixes basicly-qtmesvv). `--to` hands the claim to a holder that has written to this vault (handover).

##### 3.6 Read

A read serves the local fold (first valid claim wins) and prints the data age: fetch age, last shared event per writer, queued count and age (V5, OD1). It never waits on the network (S2, D6). Fetches happen in shares, agent hooks, the pre-push hook, the board timer and `sync`. All worktrees on a machine share one clone and queue (D1). 13 clones fetching every 20 s make 0.65 reads per second, under GitHub's 15 (sourced).

#### 4. Projects (core minimum)

- `registry init <url>`: writes the registry genesis into an empty repository.
- `member add <name>`: appends a `person` event; `member list`.
- `project add --name N --prefix P --vault <url> --code <url>`:
  - refuses equal normalized host and path, or equal root commits, for vault and code;
  - refuses a non-empty vault unless its genesis names this project;
  - pushes `project-register` like a claim (exit 0, 3 or 4); `create` under an unsettled prefix refuses; a second registration of a prefix is void and refused with the owner (P1);
  - writes the vault genesis; a rerun continues at the first missing step;
  - refuses a public vault for a private code repository (anonymous `git ls-remote`); two private repositories cannot be compared (X1).
- `attach`: resolves the registry, clones the vault, reuses `writer.id`, installs version-marked hooks, prints the session rule in use, and refuses each missing piece with its command (A3).
- Cross-project edges need `--cross`; the target id is then visible to readers of the source (X1).
- Later (S8): archive, remove, portfolio, hidden projects.

#### 5. Never forget

- **Commit-msg hook** (core). Refuses a commit with no record id and no `Record: none`; fills in ` (<id>)` when the session holds exactly one claim. Exempt: git-generated `Merge `, `Revert "`, `fixup! `, `squash! `; a revert or fixup inherits the named commit's id. Warns with the claim command when the record is not held or unsettled (V4). Offline it records a local miss. Cannot catch: `--no-verify`, a machine without `attach`, forge-side commits.
- **Audit** (`fsck --code`, slice S5a) at session start and every share, on the local code clone. Lists suggestions from `closes <id>` and reverts, merged commits with no record, `Record: none` commits, in-progress records with no code activity, and stale claims; stores `link` and `miss` events (V3, L5). After cutover it imports, by event id, ledger lines from any branch that lands with `.basicly/ledger` changes.
- **Agent hooks**: fetch and share in slice S3 (section 3.1); notices of held, stale, unsettled, taken and lost claims and suggestions in slice S6.
- **PR check** (slice S6, no token). Refuses a PR with no id shape and no `none`, and any change to `tracker.toml` other than its first add. Advisory on GitHub Free private repositories.

What slips past: a bypassed commit (a `miss`); a quiet session (old "last shared" time); an unsettled claim elsewhere (invisible until it lands).

#### 6. Visibility

- **Views**: ready, show, status (holders, blocked, stale, ready count, closed in 7 days, misses, data age; V1 per project, portfolio in S8).
- **Stale claims**: idle 2 hours (agent) or 3 days (person); flagged, never released (V2).
- **After /clear**: SessionStart lists this writer's other sessions' claims and `claim --take`.
- **Output**: versioned `--json`; no prompt or pager (D5, D7).

#### 7. Security

- **Credentials**: the user's git credentials only, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, no token written (X7); https userinfo refused (basicly-qlum6ls); `attach` prints the sign-in step on failure.
- **Untrusted text**: record text reaches an agent between `<<<record-text-<nonce>` and `record-text-<nonce>>>>` (random nonce per output, control characters stripped); nothing runs or follows it (X6).
- **Tamper detection** (X3, partly): never-retract, commit shapes, rule 2b, the author warning (section 1.1), and a released-hash check of `reader.py` and `FORMAT.md`.
- **Authority**: any `ended` on a vault head stops shares; it voids later lines only when the registry holds the same `ended`, otherwise `fsck` reports it. `config` values are bounded.
- **Board**: loopback only; state changes need a per-session token and matching Host and Origin (X8).

#### 8. Longevity

- **FORMAT.md** and **reader.py** (standard library, at most 300 lines, reads a clone or an export) ship in the wheel and genesis; T-reader compares it with the kit on clean and repaired corpora (L2).
- **Export**: `basicly-tracker export <dir>` writes the valid events with `ord`, `FORMAT.md`, `reader.py` and a SHA-256 manifest; `import <dir>` restores into an empty vault (L4). Recovery point: each writer's last share.
- **Move** (slice S9; vault or registry): `move <new-url>` pushes `ended` (reason `moved`) to the registry, then the old URL; copies history to the empty target; checks the target holds the old head. A rerun resumes; `--old-lost` starts from this clone (P4).
- **Continue** (slice S9): `ended` with reason `continued`; the successor's genesis names the predecessor.
- **Growth**: 0.64 KB per event (measured); 64 MB at 5 years (assumed 20,000 events a year).

#### 9. Install, upgrade, migration, removal

- **Install**: one README line, `uv tool install git+https://github.com/<owner>/basicly@<tag>#subdirectory=packages/basicly-tracker`, then `attach`. A gate checks documented commands against `--help` (A7).
- **Upgrade**: `basicly-tracker upgrade` prints `uv tool install --force git+https://…@<new-tag>#subdirectory=packages/basicly-tracker`; run again, it migrates state and hooks, prints both versions, resumes, refuses a downgrade (A2). `config set min-version` lists active writers not yet on it.
- **Migration** (slice S7): `basicly-tracker migrate --from ledger|beads|beans <path> --vault <url> [--preview]`, resumable. For the ledger (v7 section 11): freeze, import in fold order keeping ids, verify count and digest, write the cutover files. `--abort` before cutover unfreezes. `--branch` imports a branch's post-freeze ledger lines by event id and removes its ledger changes in one commit, so it merges cleanly. `--rollback --confirm <prefix>` after cutover pushes `ended` (reason `rolled-back`) to the registry, then the vault, then exports the vault events into the ledger with a digest check (A5).
- **Removal**: `uninstall` refuses held claims or a non-empty queue unless `--release` and `--export <file>`; `sync --from <file>` re-queues an exported queue with id dedupe (A4).
- **Platforms**: CI on Windows, macOS, Linux; spaced paths, `icacls`, PowerShell (A6).

#### 10. Recovery

Commands omit `basicly-tracker`. Each row's test injects the failure, runs the repair, and compares the fold with an unfailed control.

- R1 crash after each share step (1 to 5): `sync`. Expected: none.
- R2 torn queue tail: cut back under `LedgerLock`. Expected: the torn event is missing and reported.
- R3 host outage: claims exit 5; `sync`. Expected: none.
- R4 vault force-push or bypass merge: `fsck --repair`. Expected: other writers' holder changes become `claim-lost`.
- R5 registry force-push or loss: `fsck --repair --registry`, or `move --old-lost <url>`. Expected: none.
- R6 vault lost on the host: `move --old-lost <url>` from the freshest clone. Expected: events that clone never fetched are missing until their writers `sync`.
- R7 lost machine: `claim <id> --take --reason`. Expected: its queue is lost.
- R8 unsettled claim: `claim <id> --wait` or `--cancel`. Expected: zero or one holder.
- R9 prefix race lost: `project add` with another prefix. Expected: none.
- R10 crash in `project add` or `attach`: rerun. Expected: none.
- R11 corrupt clone: `reclone` (keeps `writer.id` and refs; refuses an unshared queue unless `--export`). Expected: none.
- R12 crash in `move` or `migrate`: rerun (or `migrate --abort`). Expected: none.
- R13 cutover regretted: `migrate --rollback`. Expected: the vault ends; the ledger equals the vault fold.
- R14 web edit of an old line: that commit is quarantined. Expected: a report line only.

#### 11. Proof tests

Local CI: bare repositories, push 1.5 s and fetch 0.5 s injected. Probes: private GitHub repositories basicly-testbed (code), basicly-testbed-registry and basicly-testbed-vault.

Each test: input, action, pass; anything else fails.

- T-claim-gate (gates S4): 52 sessions on 13 machines run the real `claim`, time scaled 4 times as in sim.py, seeds 1 to 3, 30 scaled minutes each (about 230 claims, 25 minutes wall time). Pass: every claim ends 0 or 3 within 60 s, no exit 4, one holder per record, p99 at most 10 s (corrected 2026-11-12 from p95 to the owner's D1 number, decided by the orchestrator).
- T-claim-load (nightly; gates only the S7 cutover): full time, 6 runs of 70 minutes, seeds 1 to 6, at least 1,000 claims. Pass: as T-claim-gate, plus p99 at most 10 s (measured per run 4.2 to 8.3 s), mean at most 6 push attempts per minute, busiest minute at most 24 (measured 12 to 18, plus a third).
- T-claim-burst: 13 claims in one second, one fetch stalled 40 s. Pass: answers within 30 s; all end 0 or 3 within 60 s.
- T-exclusive: 3 clones, and 8 sessions in one, claim one record. Pass: one exit 0, the rest 3.
- T-bulk (gates S7): 52 sessions on 13 clones, 10 bulk events per session per hour, prompt hook every 2 minutes (assumed), 70 minutes, seed 1; a reader clone hooks every 30 s. Pass: p95 visibility at most 240 s; Stop empties every queue.
- T-fork: bypass merges, force-pushes, forged lines, web edits, `ended`. Pass: no silent retraction; a bad commit voids only itself; nothing counts after `ended`; two repairs give one copy.
- T-writers (S3): 16 local processes plus 50 clones, 10,000 events. Pass: each once.
- T-storage (S1): 50 live and 200 retired writers, 1,000,000 events, archive on. Pass: pack at most 0.7 GB (normal repack); under 1,000 files.
- T-clone5y (S8): 100,000 events. Pass: pack at most 70 MB; clone at most 60 s at 10 Mbit/s.
- T-flaky (S7): remote gone 10 minutes, one git call stalled. Pass: no command over its deadline; the next hook shares the queue once.
- T-expiry: injected clock; an unsettled claim aged 10 minutes, landed or not. Pass: dropped, or unassigned if landed.
- T-hook: messages with an id, `none`, nothing, `Merge`, `Revert "`, `fixup!`. Pass: only the third refused; the revert inherits the id.
- T-layers: AST scan. Pass: no forbidden import or `os.environ` below adapters.
- T-wrong-use: each refusal in sections 3 to 9. Pass: exit code, cause, next command, no state change.
- T-exit: each exit code. Pass: its printed next command runs.
- T-no-code-write (N1, C2): 1,000 tracker writes. Pass: the code repository's `git status --porcelain` is empty.
- T-agents (N2): 8 sessions in 3 worktrees, 1,000 events. Pass: each once; no lock wait over 1 s.
- T-audit (N3): commit with no id via `--no-verify`, direct push, `closes <id>`. Pass: one `miss` each and one suggestion.
- T-visible (gates S7; N4, V5): A comments and runs Stop; B runs SessionStart, then `status`. Pass: B shows the comment with a data age under 30 s.
- T-seen (C2): B fetches W's commit; W's commit is force-pushed away. Pass: B refuses to share, naming `fsck --repair`; repair restores W's lines in a `requeue`; `reclone` keeps the refs.
- T-ended (C3): rollback crashes after the registry push. Pass: every clone stops sharing at its next fetch, keeps its queue, and nothing lands after `ended`.
- T-urgent-retry (C5): 13 claims in one second, injected latency. Pass: no claim stops before 13 attempts unless its 30 s deadline passed.
- T-refspec (C6): a fresh bare clone fetches after a new commit. Pass: `refs/remotes/origin/main` moves to the new head.
- T-fetch-lock (C7): two fetches at once, one stalled 5 s. Pass: no `cannot lock ref`; the head never moves back.
- T-branch (C4): a pre-freeze branch appends to `.basicly/ledger`; `migrate --branch`, then merge. Pass: no conflict; each line once in the vault.
- T-late-ledger (C4): a branch merged after cutover adds `pending-<writer>.jsonl`. Pass: `fsck --code` imports each line once; a second run imports nothing.
- T-redact: a wheel write with a token and a path. Pass: neither is queued.
- T-plain (C3): Pass: tracker data is only on default branches of the registry and vault; no refs, notes or branches are pushed.
- R1 to R14: as section 10.
- P-claim: 13 clones, 2 hours, basicly-testbed-vault. Pass: p99 at most 10 s; mean at most 6 pushes per minute; no HTTP 429 or secondary rate limit; push latency at most twice idle.
- P-visibility: public and private pairs. Pass: right answer in 10 s, no prompt.
- P-session: a session, its subagent, SessionEnd. Pass: one `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; SessionEnd runs `sync`. Rerun each Claude Code release.
- P-merge (N1): two code PRs with tracker writes. Pass: both mergeable after one merges.
- P-size: after P-claim. Pass: GitHub's reported size within 20 % of the local pack.

### Share commit identity (added 2026-11-12, decided by the orchestrator)

Share commits are unsigned and authored by the writer id (name: the first 12 characters, email: the writer id at writers.basicly.invalid); no personal name or email enters a vault. The tool sets commit.gpgSign=false and an empty core.hooksPath per command, only in its own vault clone, and never writes them to the global or a code-repository config. If the vault repository requires signed commits on the forge, the push is refused and the share stops at once with a message that names the cause and the setting to turn off.

### Local refs and C3 (added 2026-11-12, decided by the orchestrator, owner to confirm)

The tool keeps refs/basicly/seen and refs/basicly/retracted/N only in its own local vault clone as a recovery copy. It never pushes them, fsck --repair puts every recoverable line back in ordinary files, and fsck, doctor and uninstall show or remove them. So no tracker fact is hidden on the forge or lives only in a ref after a repair, which keeps C3.

Base: design version 7 ("v7", record basicly-gtb19bg.60). Measured facts: verify/RESULTS.md. Every command is `basicly-tracker` (packages/basicly-tracker/pyproject.toml:13). Hosts: GitHub only in the core (OD6); the format names no host.

#### 0. Overview

1. One small registry repository lists projects and owns every prefix.
2. One vault repository per project holds the backlog; it is the unit of read access.
3. Each machine has one bare clone per vault, a writer id kept in its state folder, and a queue beside the clone.
4. A write appends to the queue; a share pushes one commit built on the fetched head.
5. Claim, take and unassign push at once (a plain push is the compare-and-swap); other events wait for a bulk slot.
6. Order is first-parent commit order; git stores it once; an export writes it into each line.
7. A clone never retracts a commit it has seen; a rewrite stops shares until `fsck --repair`.
8. Code never changes a status; hooks and an audit link the tracker to the code.
9. Every view prints the data age.
10. A vault ends only with a stop event that names its successor.

Bad news first.

- Five or more claims in one second can take over 10 s (measured: 9 of 13, maximum 26.5 s).
- Any writer with push rights can write lines in another writer's name until identity binding (OD2) exists. X3 is partly met.

#### 1. Decisions

##### 1.1 Owner answers of 2026-11-12 (binding)

Owner decisions are OD1 to OD6 here, apart from requirement ids D1 to D7.

- **OD1, N4.** Claims answered within 10 s at p99; other events within about 4 minutes (1.2 T at 13 machines is 234 s); every view shows the data age.
- **OD2, identity binding (X2) and OD3, erasure (X5)**: deferred.
- **OD4, forecast (V6)**: waits until M5 is cut over.
- **OD5**: the commit hook refuses a commit with no record id (section 5). **OD6**: GitHub only in the core. **Core first**: S2b, S3, S4, S2c, S5a, S7 (section 12).

What a reader sees under the deferred OD2: when a writer id pushes under a commit author it never used before, `fsck` prints `writer <id> (<name>) pushed commit <sha> as <new author>; first seen as <old author>`. That line shows in every view's warning block and in the portfolio until a person runs `fsck --ack-author <id> <author>`. The events still count.

##### 1.2 SPEC.md rules that a vault retires or changes

For a vault, FORMAT.md replaces these rules; after cutover the old ledger is only a `migrate` source.

#### 2. Data

##### 2.1 Layer map

| Layer | Contents | May import |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kit (pure) | format, commit-shape check, fold, holder verdicts, config fold, budget arithmetic | standard library; no network, subprocess or environment |
| Transport | `git_runner.py` (the only subprocess), clone, fetch, share, deadlines, code-history reader | kit |
| Adapters | CLI, commit hook, agent hooks, board, CI template | transport, kit |

Only adapters read the environment. Slice S2b makes `environ` a required argument of `holders.py:80`, `writers.py:23` and `events.py:759-779`. T-layers enforces this.

##### 2.2 Repositories

- **Registry**: one per tracker; it owns every prefix. Events: `registry-created`, `person`, `project-register`, `prefix-alias`, `project-archive`, `ended`.
- **Vault**: one per project. Both start with a genesis commit; `vault.toml` (own uid, kind, registry uid, project uid) is read from genesis only.
- **Configuration is events**: bounded `config` events set bulk constants, minimum version, stale times, statuses and fields (P5).
- **Code repository**: `.basicly/tracker.toml` (registry uid, project uid) and one README line with the registry URL (C2, C3).
- **Machine state folder** (mode 0700; `icacls` on Windows): `writer.id` (kept across reclones); per vault `clone/` (bare), `queue.jsonl`, `sessions.json`, `log/`. The registry URL (state folder, README line or `attach --registry <url>`) is accepted only when its genesis uid matches `tracker.toml`.

##### 2.3 Ids and sessions

- Registry, vault, project, writer and person ids: random 128-bit (P2, P4).
- Event id: writer id plus 128 random bits, fixed at queue time. `link`, `miss` and `claim-lost` ids are content hashes.
- Record id: `<prefix>-<root>.<n>` (SPEC.md 9.4). A rename adds an alias; the old prefix stays owned (P3).
- Holder: (writer id, session id). Session id, first match wins: (1) `--session <id>` minted by this clone; (2) `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; (3) `BASICLY_TRACKER_SESSION` from `session new`; (4) the machine's person session. Rule 4 is refused when an agent marker variable is set (assumed; P-session), so two agents never share a holder (D3).

##### 2.4 Files

Layout: `log/<writer-id>/<nnnnn>.jsonl`; the first line of a segment is the writer header. A new segment starts at 1.5 MB: files of 1.39 MB cost 640 B per event, files of 7.3 MB cost 3.3 KB (measured, normal repack, verify/storage).

An archive commit packs the open tails of writers idle for 90 days into `log/archive/<nnnnn>.jsonl`, byte for byte. At 1,000,000 events of 1.39 KB: 927 full segments, 50 live tails, 1 archive tail, about 978 files (arithmetic; T-storage decides).

##### 2.5 Event format and commit shapes

```text
{"v":1,"id":"…","ts":"2026-11-12T09:00:00Z","project":"…","record":"abc-k3x9.2",
 "kind":"claim","writer":"…","session":"…","via":"agent","actor":"<person id>","payload":{}}
```

- Every release reads every earlier `v` (L1). `ts` is UTC RFC 3339, evidence only (L6). `actor` is the responsible person (D4).
- Unknown kinds and fields are kept and skipped. A kind that changes holders or status carries `"fold":true`; an old tool meeting an unknown one refuses holder commands on that record and names the upgrade (A1).
- **Stop kind** (reserved in v1): `ended`, with `reason` (`moved`, `continued`, `rolled-back`), successor URL and uid. Every v1 tool refuses writes to a repository that holds a valid `ended`.

**One validity rule.** A clone reads the default branch in first-parent order and takes each line's bytes from the commit that added it. Each commit has one shape:

1. **Genesis**: no parent; adds exactly `vault.toml`, `FORMAT.md`, `reader.py`, `README.md`.
2. **Format**: one parent; changes only `FORMAT.md`, `reader.py` or `README.md`; carries no events.
3. **Batch**: one parent; only appends lines under `log/<w>/` for one writer `w`; a new segment starts with a header naming `w`; (2b) every event line's `writer` is `w`; no line is changed or removed.
4. **Archive**: one parent; moves whole files verbatim into `log/archive/`; the clone checks the bytes.

Any other commit is quarantined alone and reported. Nothing after a valid `ended` counts. Order is commit order, then line order; exports write it as `ord`. A git clone or an export is the portable form; files without history are readable but unordered.

**Fetch.** One fetch lock per clone serializes fetches. The bare clone fetches `+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`; the head is `refs/remotes/origin/main`. A failed fetch is retried once; then the command uses the last state and prints its age.

**Never retract.** The clone keeps local refs `refs/basicly/seen` and `refs/basicly/retracted/<n>` (never pushed, safe from `gc`). After every fetch, if the head's first-parent chain lacks the seen tip, the clone marks it retracted, refuses to share, and names `basicly-tracker fsck --repair`; otherwise it validates the new commits and moves `refs/basicly/seen` to the head. `reclone` copies both refs into the new clone.

**Repair.** `fsck --repair` re-queues every line on a retracted ref that is not valid on the head: own lines as they were, other writers' lines inside one `requeue` event that keeps their ids and changes no holder. A claim that no longer holds gets a `claim-lost` event, shown to its holder at the next hook and command. `fsck --accept-rewrite <head> --purge` drops retracted refs for a deliberate purge.

#### 3. Write, share and read

##### 3.1 Write

A command redacts secrets and absolute paths with a standard-library redactor that ships in the wheel (new in slice S3; X4) and runs on every write path, appends to `queue.jsonl` under `LedgerLock` with `fsync`, and prints `shared` or `queued (<n> events, oldest <age>); shares at your next tracker command or hook`. With `CI` or `BASICLY_TRACKER_EPHEMERAL` set, every write shares at once. Core agent hooks (slice S3): SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit fetch (3 s deadline, at most every 20 s) and run a due share; Stop and SessionEnd share the whole queue (SessionEnd assumed; P-session).

##### 3.2 Share

Under the share lock, plumbing only:

1. Fetch (section 2.5). If the head holds any valid `ended`, stop: keep the queue, and for `moved` or `continued` re-target it to the successor; `rolled-back` has no successor, so the command prints that the project rolled back and keeps the queue for `uninstall --export`.
2. Drop queued events whose ids are valid on the head.
3. Build the commit on the head with `hash-object`, a temporary index, `write-tree` and `commit-tree`; a crash leaves only unreferenced objects.
4. Push plainly. On refusal, go to step 1: an urgent share retries until the 30 s claim deadline; a bulk share retries at most 5 times.
5. On success, move `refs/basicly/seen`, then remove the shared events from the queue under `LedgerLock`.

A share sends its starting queue plus one more pass (v7 drain bound).

##### 3.3 Push budget

- **Urgent**: claim, take, unassign, project register. They push at once and carry the whole queue.
- **Bulk**: all others. They ride on an urgent push, or share at the first trigger after `T = max(60 s, M × 60 / 4)` times a random 0.8 to 1.2 (the simulated rule, sim.py:144-146). M is the number of writers with a commit in the last hour.
- **Triggers**: every command, every agent hook, the commit and pre-push hooks, the board every 30 s.
- **Bursts**: one clone per machine puts its sessions' claims into one push; nothing more is promised (S4 not met for 5 or more claims in one second).

##### 3.4 Claim protocol

`basicly-tracker claim <id>` has one 30 s deadline; each git call gets only the time that remains.

1. Validate the id and session (section 2.3). Missing: exit 1.
2. `git ls-remote`, at most 5 s. No answer: exit 5; nothing is queued.
3. Fetch and fold. Held by this session: exit 7. Held by another session: exit 3, with no push.
4. Append the claim to the queue and share. Another session on this machine may push it; that counts the same.
5. When the claim is valid on the head, fold. First claim: exit 0. Otherwise: exit 3.
6. Deadline: exit 4, "unsettled: do not start work; run basicly-tracker claim <id> --wait, or --cancel".

An unsettled claim is never held; the next command or core hook retries it. `claim <id> --cancel` takes the share lock, fetches, and drops the claim, or unassigns it if it landed. After 10 minutes it expires the same way.

Exit codes for every command, with the next command printed: 0 done; 1 refused by name, with the fix; 2 usage, `--help`; 3 held by another session, `claim <id> --take --reason "<text>"`; 4 unsettled, `--wait` or `--cancel`; 5 offline, `git ls-remote <url>` then retry; 6 internal error without traceback, the log path and `sync` (`doctor` from slice S10); 7 already held by this session.

##### 3.5 Holder changes

- `claim <id> --take --reason <text>` refuses a fresh claim unless `--force`. Without `--reason` it works only on a same-writer session idle for 30 minutes in `sessions.json`: resume after `/clear` (D2). Every take is logged; the old holder sees "taken by <name>: <reason>" at its next hook.
- `unassign <id> [--to <holder>]` is valid only from the holder (fixes basicly-qtmesvv). `--to` hands the claim to a holder that has written to this vault (handover).

##### 3.6 Read

A read serves the local fold (first valid claim wins) and prints the data age: fetch age, last shared event per writer, queued count and age (V5, OD1). It never waits on the network (S2, D6). Fetches happen in shares, agent hooks, the pre-push hook, the board timer and `sync`. All worktrees on a machine share one clone and queue (D1). 13 clones fetching every 20 s make 0.65 reads per second, under GitHub's 15 (sourced).

#### 4. Projects (core minimum)

- `registry init <url>`: writes the registry genesis into an empty repository.
- `member add <name>`: appends a `person` event; `member list`.
- `project add --name N --prefix P --vault <url> --code <url>`:
  - refuses equal normalized host and path, or equal root commits, for vault and code;
  - refuses a non-empty vault unless its genesis names this project;
  - pushes `project-register` like a claim (exit 0, 3 or 4); `create` under an unsettled prefix refuses; a second registration of a prefix is void and refused with the owner (P1);
  - writes the vault genesis; a rerun continues at the first missing step;
  - refuses a public vault for a private code repository (anonymous `git ls-remote`); two private repositories cannot be compared (X1).
- `attach`: resolves the registry, clones the vault, reuses `writer.id`, installs version-marked hooks, prints the session rule in use, and refuses each missing piece with its command (A3).
- Cross-project edges need `--cross`; the target id is then visible to readers of the source (X1).
- Later (S8): archive, remove, portfolio, hidden projects.

#### 5. Never forget

- **Commit-msg hook** (core). Refuses a commit with no record id and no `Record: none`; fills in ` (<id>)` when the session holds exactly one claim. Exempt: git-generated `Merge `, `Revert "`, `fixup! `, `squash! `; a revert or fixup inherits the named commit's id. Warns with the claim command when the record is not held or unsettled (V4). Offline it records a local miss. Cannot catch: `--no-verify`, a machine without `attach`, forge-side commits.
- **Audit** (`fsck --code`, slice S5a) at session start and every share, on the local code clone. Lists suggestions from `closes <id>` and reverts, merged commits with no record, `Record: none` commits, in-progress records with no code activity, and stale claims; stores `link` and `miss` events (V3, L5). After cutover it imports, by event id, ledger lines from any branch that lands with `.basicly/ledger` changes.
- **Agent hooks**: fetch and share in slice S3 (section 3.1); notices of held, stale, unsettled, taken and lost claims and suggestions in slice S6.
- **PR check** (slice S6, no token). Refuses a PR with no id shape and no `none`, and any change to `tracker.toml` other than its first add. Advisory on GitHub Free private repositories.

What slips past: a bypassed commit (a `miss`); a quiet session (old "last shared" time); an unsettled claim elsewhere (invisible until it lands).

#### 6. Visibility

- **Views**: ready, show, status (holders, blocked, stale, ready count, closed in 7 days, misses, data age; V1 per project, portfolio in S8).
- **Stale claims**: idle 2 hours (agent) or 3 days (person); flagged, never released (V2).
- **After /clear**: SessionStart lists this writer's other sessions' claims and `claim --take`.
- **Output**: versioned `--json`; no prompt or pager (D5, D7).

#### 7. Security

- **Credentials**: the user's git credentials only, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, no token written (X7); https userinfo refused (basicly-qlum6ls); `attach` prints the sign-in step on failure.
- **Untrusted text**: record text reaches an agent between `<<<record-text-<nonce>` and `record-text-<nonce>>>>` (random nonce per output, control characters stripped); nothing runs or follows it (X6).
- **Tamper detection** (X3, partly): never-retract, commit shapes, rule 2b, the author warning (section 1.1), and a released-hash check of `reader.py` and `FORMAT.md`.
- **Authority**: any `ended` on a vault head stops shares; it voids later lines only when the registry holds the same `ended`, otherwise `fsck` reports it. `config` values are bounded.
- **Board**: loopback only; state changes need a per-session token and matching Host and Origin (X8).

#### 8. Longevity

- **FORMAT.md** and **reader.py** (standard library, at most 300 lines, reads a clone or an export) ship in the wheel and genesis; T-reader compares it with the kit on clean and repaired corpora (L2).
- **Export**: `basicly-tracker export <dir>` writes the valid events with `ord`, `FORMAT.md`, `reader.py` and a SHA-256 manifest; `import <dir>` restores into an empty vault (L4). Recovery point: each writer's last share.
- **Move** (slice S9; vault or registry): `move <new-url>` pushes `ended` (reason `moved`) to the registry, then the old URL; copies history to the empty target; checks the target holds the old head. A rerun resumes; `--old-lost` starts from this clone (P4).
- **Continue** (slice S9): `ended` with reason `continued`; the successor's genesis names the predecessor.
- **Growth**: 0.64 KB per event (measured); 64 MB at 5 years (assumed 20,000 events a year).

#### 9. Install, upgrade, migration, removal

- **Install**: one README line, `uv tool install git+https://github.com/<owner>/basicly@<tag>#subdirectory=packages/basicly-tracker`, then `attach`. A gate checks documented commands against `--help` (A7).
- **Upgrade**: `basicly-tracker upgrade` prints `uv tool install --force git+https://…@<new-tag>#subdirectory=packages/basicly-tracker`; run again, it migrates state and hooks, prints both versions, resumes, refuses a downgrade (A2). `config set min-version` lists active writers not yet on it.
- **Migration** (slice S7): `basicly-tracker migrate --from ledger|beads|beans <path> --vault <url> [--preview]`, resumable. For the ledger (v7 section 11): freeze, import in fold order keeping ids, verify count and digest, write the cutover files. `--abort` before cutover unfreezes. `--branch` imports a branch's post-freeze ledger lines by event id and removes its ledger changes in one commit, so it merges cleanly. `--rollback --confirm <prefix>` after cutover pushes `ended` (reason `rolled-back`) to the registry, then the vault, then exports the vault events into the ledger with a digest check (A5).
- **Removal**: `uninstall` refuses held claims or a non-empty queue unless `--release` and `--export <file>`; `sync --from <file>` re-queues an exported queue with id dedupe (A4).
- **Platforms**: CI on Windows, macOS, Linux; spaced paths, `icacls`, PowerShell (A6).

#### 10. Recovery

Commands omit `basicly-tracker`. Each row's test injects the failure, runs the repair, and compares the fold with an unfailed control.

- R1 crash after each share step (1 to 5): `sync`. Expected: none.
- R2 torn queue tail: cut back under `LedgerLock`. Expected: the torn event is missing and reported.
- R3 host outage: claims exit 5; `sync`. Expected: none.
- R4 vault force-push or bypass merge: `fsck --repair`. Expected: other writers' holder changes become `claim-lost`.
- R5 registry force-push or loss: `fsck --repair --registry`, or `move --old-lost <url>`. Expected: none.
- R6 vault lost on the host: `move --old-lost <url>` from the freshest clone. Expected: events that clone never fetched are missing until their writers `sync`.
- R7 lost machine: `claim <id> --take --reason`. Expected: its queue is lost.
- R8 unsettled claim: `claim <id> --wait` or `--cancel`. Expected: zero or one holder.
- R9 prefix race lost: `project add` with another prefix. Expected: none.
- R10 crash in `project add` or `attach`: rerun. Expected: none.
- R11 corrupt clone: `reclone` (keeps `writer.id` and refs; refuses an unshared queue unless `--export`). Expected: none.
- R12 crash in `move` or `migrate`: rerun (or `migrate --abort`). Expected: none.
- R13 cutover regretted: `migrate --rollback`. Expected: the vault ends; the ledger equals the vault fold.
- R14 web edit of an old line: that commit is quarantined. Expected: a report line only.

#### 11. Proof tests

Local CI: bare repositories, push 1.5 s and fetch 0.5 s injected. Probes: private GitHub repositories basicly-testbed (code), basicly-testbed-registry and basicly-testbed-vault.

Each test: input, action, pass; anything else fails.

- T-claim-gate (gates S4): 52 sessions on 13 machines run the real `claim`, time scaled 4 times as in sim.py, seeds 1 to 3, 30 scaled minutes each (about 230 claims, 25 minutes wall time). Pass: every claim ends 0 or 3 within 60 s, no exit 4, one holder per record, p99 at most 10 s (corrected 2026-11-12 from p95 to the owner's D1 number, decided by the orchestrator).
- T-claim-load (nightly; gates only the S7 cutover): full time, 6 runs of 70 minutes, seeds 1 to 6, at least 1,000 claims. Pass: as T-claim-gate, plus p99 at most 10 s (measured per run 4.2 to 8.3 s), mean at most 6 push attempts per minute, busiest minute at most 24 (measured 12 to 18, plus a third).
- T-claim-burst: 13 claims in one second, one fetch stalled 40 s. Pass: answers within 30 s; all end 0 or 3 within 60 s.

- T-writers (S3): 16 local processes plus 50 clones, 10,000 events. Pass: each once.
- T-storage (S1): 50 live and 200 retired writers, 1,000,000 events, archive on. Pass: pack at most 0.7 GB (normal repack); under 1,000 files.
- T-clone5y (S8): 100,000 events. Pass: pack at most 70 MB; clone at most 60 s at 10 Mbit/s.

- T-no-code-write (N1, C2): 1,000 tracker writes. Pass: the code repository's `git status --porcelain` is empty.
- T-agents (N2): 8 sessions in 3 worktrees, 1,000 events. Pass: each once; no lock wait over 1 s.
- T-audit (N3): commit with no id via `--no-verify`, direct push, `closes <id>`. Pass: one `miss` each and one suggestion.
- T-visible (gates S7; N4, V5): A comments and runs Stop; B runs SessionStart, then `status`. Pass: B shows the comment with a data age under 30 s.

Slices S2b to S4 change and need approval. Core, in order; S3 and S4 tests create vaults with test fixtures:

### Share commit identity (added 2026-11-12, decided by the orchestrator)

Share commits are unsigned and authored by the writer id (name: the first 12 characters, email: the writer id at writers.basicly.invalid); no personal name or email enters a vault. The tool sets commit.gpgSign=false and an empty core.hooksPath per command, only in its own vault clone, and never writes them to the global or a code-repository config. If the vault repository requires signed commits on the forge, the push is refused and the share stops at once with a message that names the cause and the setting to turn off.

### Local refs and C3 (added 2026-11-12, decided by the orchestrator, owner to confirm)

The tool keeps refs/basicly/seen and refs/basicly/retracted/N only in its own local vault clone as a recovery copy. It never pushes them, fsck --repair puts every recoverable line back in ordinary files, and fsck, doctor and uninstall show or remove them. So no tracker fact is hidden on the forge or lives only in a ref after a repair, which keeps C3.

### Push rate (added 2026-11-12, decided by the orchestrator)

GitHub documents "Push rate: The recommended maximum limit is 6 pushes per minute per repository" under Activity, introduced as "To avoid throttling and performance issues, we recommend staying within the following operational limits" (docs.github.com repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/repository-limits, read 2026-11-12). It is guidance, not an enforced limit; the page names no rejection above it. Requirement not met at 52 sessions: the scale 1 claim gate at the design rate measured 9.03 pushes per minute on average and 18 in the busiest minute, because each claim pushes alone. Pushes per minute is reported in every run and not gated. The nightly T-claim-load at about twice the design rate gates safety only (no two holders, every claim answered within 30 s, no exit 4, 5 or 6), because it tests a load beyond the design; the design-rate gate keeps p99 at most 10 s.

payload.description:
## Context

Almost every number that governs the factory is currently set by judgment and then never
revisited against what actually happened. The one exception proved the point twice in a single
session: the first measured lane actual (4079243 tokens, 3.657368 USD, 519.6s) corrected a cost
estimate that was wrong by ~2.4x, and then supplied the bound that basicly-vz78 needed. Both were
decisions a measurement changed. Nothing else in the config has that feedback loop.

The owner's framing (2026-08-01): the per-lane budget is changeable, so it should be *learned*
rather than set — and the same applies to the other parameters. Gather the observations, pair them
with the parameters in force, and let the configuration adapt to evidence.

There is already scaffolding to build on rather than invent: run records carry per-dispatch facts,
`decompose.calibrated_build_factors` already replaces its seeds from measured samples past
`calibration_min_samples`, `run_record.SpendCalibration` already keeps a measured ratio beside the
prior it displaced, and `WaitEvent` already meters human wait. This bead is about extending that
pattern to the parameters that have no loop yet, and about making the resulting recommendation
readable.

## The parameters that are currently guesses

- `[runner] runner_timeout` - the owner's example. Set to 1800 today as a cost control, with no
  evidence about what value maximises landed work per token.
- `[worktree] concurrency` - now 5, exercised at 1. Throughput against tracker-write and CPU
  contention is exactly an empirical question.
- `[runner] max_agent_processes`, `stall_after`
- `[sizing] working_set_min` / `working_set_max` - the band that refuses a package
- `[sizing] build_factors` per task class, `context_ceiling`, `calibration_min_samples`,
  `calibration_window`
- `[policy] max_rework`, `max_subtasks_per_lane`, `decider_max_decisions`
- `decompose.UNSIZED_LANE_TOKENS_SEED` and the choice of statistic behind
  `unsized_lane_tokens` (median today, chosen against a bimodal sample of 13 - see basicly-vz78)

## Observations to record per dispatch, so the above can be learned

Outcome signals (what "best results" means, and it is not one number):

- landed on the first attempt, versus rework consumed before landing
- gate failures per lane, split deterministic versus flaky (a flake distorts every other
  measurement - basicly-5h0g, basicly-55yh)
- tokens, cost, wall clock (recorded today)
- final context occupancy against `context_ceiling`, and whether the overrun follow-up fired
- whether the lane hit `runner_timeout`, and what it had produced when it did
- whether it wrote `needs-input.json`, and on what class of missing fact
- declared scope versus files actually touched (relates to basicly-jr0l.44)
- merge-queue events: bounces, D5 base-moved cancellations, retries
- human interventions with cause and kind, and the wait each one cost (`WaitEvent.waited_s`)
- forecast against actual, once basicly-vz78 makes pairs obtainable at all

Each observation has to be stored beside **the parameter values in force for that dispatch**, or
the pairing cannot be reconstructed later - which is the same mistake that left 5 forecasts and 13
actuals with no pair between them.

## Constraints this must respect

- **Advisory, not self-modifying.** Deterministic checks block, judged checks advise, and the
  engine disposes. A tuner proposes a configuration change and reports the evidence; a human or a
  gate applies it. Nothing here may rewrite `basicly.toml` on its own.
- Recommendations must name their sample size and never present a seed as a measurement, the way
  `SpendCalibration` already does.
- Telemetry that never leaves the machine is half useless: `.basicly/usage/` is self-ignored, so a
  measurement that should inform a shared decision has to reach the tracker (basicly-kjc5.50 made
  calibration read both).
- No new runtime product dependency; this is arithmetic over records we already write.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a corpus of recorded dispatches when the operator asks for a tuning report then it names,
  per governed parameter, the value in force, the outcome distribution observed under it, a
  recommended value with its sample size, and whether the recommendation is measured or seeded -
  and it changes no configuration itself
payload.title: Learn the factory parameters from recorded outcomes instead of setting them by judgment

payload.description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a corpus of recorded dispatches when the operator asks for a tuning report then it names, per governed parameter, the value in force for the dispatches it summarises, the outcome distribution observed under that value, a recommended value with its sample size, and whether the recommendation is measured or seeded
- Given a governed parameter whose observed sample is smaller than the calibration minimum when the report is produced then the recommendation for that parameter is labelled seeded and reports the prior it would displace, never presenting a seed as a measurement
- Given a tuning report run when it completes then basicly.toml and every other configuration file are byte-identical to before the run, and the report only proposes changes for a human or a gate to apply
- Given dispatch observations recorded only under .basicly/usage/ and observations reachable from the tracker when the report is produced then both corpora are read and the report states which source each sample came from
- Given a corpus with no recorded dispatches for a governed parameter when the report is produced then that parameter is still listed with its value in force, a sample size of zero, and no recommendation, rather than being omitted

## Scope

- `src/basicly/tuning.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_tuning.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`

CORRECTION to my escalation answer earlier today. I answered 'retry' calling this a transient gate failure of the basicly-55yh class. That was WRONG and a future reader should not inherit it. The retry reproduced the failure identically.

The real cause, with the gate's own output which I had not read when I answered:

  Missing layer in container 'basicly': module basicly.tuning does not exist.

This is basicly-69az's mechanism on a second config surface. Verified at main:
- .importlinter is the contract file, and this lane's diff adds tuning to a layer line ('policy | tuning | verify').
- The lane adds src/basicly/tuning.py. Base does not have that file; the worktree does.
- The landing runs verify from the base checkout, whose resolved basicly package has no tuning module, while reading the lane tree's .importlinter which declares one. The contract therefore names a module the analyzed package lacks.

Same shape as 69az - a declaration in the lane's tree referencing something only the lane's code provides, validated by the pre-merge process - but 69az's fix (_tree_schema reading the tree's config.py via ast, landed today at a90585f) covers basicly.toml only and does not reach import-linter.

Why my worktree verify passed and the landing did not: 'uv run basicly verify --mode full' inside the worktree resolves the worktree's own package, which has tuning.py. That is why the tree looked green to me and not to the landing. Running the gate from the same place the landing runs it is the check I skipped.

My process error, recorded so the lesson is not lost: I formed a hypothesis (leaked VIRTUAL_ENV), tested and refuted it, and then concluded 'transient' instead of reading the gate's actual output, which was in the log I already had.

payload.description:
## The defect

The landing path has TWO merge call sites and only one records a `change-summary`. So a repair that re-lands leaves the artifact describing the superseded landing, which is the same defect `basicly-gvlpxm` fixed, reached by the other route.

- `loop._verify_and_land` merges and then calls `_record_change_summary`, which after `basicly-gvlpxm` correctly records `result.landed_head`.
- `loop._repair_from_validate` calls `merge.merge_worktree` directly and then `_dispatch_validation`. It never calls `_record_change_summary`. Nothing re-records the artifact for the merge it just performed.

The consequence is precise, because the artifact's own docstring states its contract: it is written "at the one point where the build is finished and the branch facts still exist". After a repair re-land, the recorded head, path count and digest describe the FIRST landing, and `basicly-gvlpxm`'s defect statement applies again word for word: its count and digest describe a tree that is not what landed.

## Observed, on gvlpxm's own repair landing

The repair for `basicly-gvlpxm` was committed as `c536d56f`, rebased to `be36146b`, gained a regeneration commit `6799e757`, and merged as `7381a145`. main advanced. The artifact on the record still reads:

- `commit`: `d3422f8175ddf0f60fda96b60d01abe2d0b48b5f`, the pre-rebase head of the ORIGINAL landing
- `self_check.detail`: `merged harness/basicly-gvlpxm into main @ 9534ca05`, the original merge base

Neither value describes the landing that actually put the fix in main. The fix's own re-land demonstrated the sibling gap.

## Why this is not a duplicate of gvlpxm

`basicly-gvlpxm` fixed WHICH head is read at the site that records. This record is about a merge site that does not record at all. Fixing the first cannot fix the second, and the repo rule is root cause not symptom: check other call sites before calling a single-site patch complete. The other call site was not checked, and this is it.

## The design question this must answer, not assume

Whether a repair re-land SHOULD re-record BUILD's artifact. Two readings and this record does not choose:

- It should. The artifact's contract is that it describes what landed, and after a re-land it does not. `handoff.record` is content addressed rather than write once, so a corrected payload records as a second artifact event and nothing is overwritten.
- It should not, and instead the phase model is wrong to let a merge happen outside the state that owns the artifact. `_repair_from_validate`'s docstring says the phase deliberately does not fall back to build, because that would hand the unit a phase whose work base already holds. If the artifact belongs to build, a merge outside build is the anomaly.

Whichever is chosen, an artifact that silently describes a superseded tree is the outcome to refuse.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take a record at phase `validate` whose `validate-as-consumer` gate failed and whose worktree branch carries a repair commit base does not hold.
2. Read its `change-summary` artifact and note the recorded `commit`.
3. Run `basicly loop advance <id>`.
4. Observe `_repair_from_validate` merge the branch, and observe main advance to a new head.
5. Read the `change-summary` artifact again.
6. Observe the recorded `commit` is unchanged and still names the pre-repair head, so it describes a tree that is not what landed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a repair that re-lands from validate when the merge succeeds then the change summary records the head that merge took rather than the earlier landing's head - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_handoff_states.py -k repair_reland -q`
- Given a repair re-land that fails to merge then no change summary is recorded for it and the existing artifact is left as it was - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_handoff_states.py -k repair_reland_failed -q`

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_handoff_states.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_handoff_states.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_handoff_states.py -k repair_reland -q`
payload.title: a repair re-land merges without recording a change summary so the artifact describes a superseded tree

payload.text:
Closed by 6e89b80d. Full verify PASS, 31 checks, 4488 tests.

_repair_from_validate now reads the changed paths before the merge and calls _record_change_summary after a successful one. A failed merge records nothing.

This record posed a design question and declined to answer it. Its ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA answer it - record the head the merge took - and the reasoning holds on its own terms: handoff.record is content addressed rather than write once, so the corrected payload is a second event and nothing is overwritten. I followed the criteria and am naming that the record's prose and its criteria disagreed about whether a choice had been made.

Nothing exercised this path at all. A search of tests/ for _repair_from_validate's own block message returns nothing, against a positive control finding the string at loop.py:518. That is why the missing call survived two records about the same artifact.

My first test pair did not discriminate. Mutation 2 - reading the changed paths AFTER the merge, the ordering _changed_paths' own docstring forbids - PASSED, because _pin_landing pins branch_changed_paths to a constant so before and after are identical. The changed set now differs across the merge by injection, so when it is read is observable, and that mutation fails. Both mutations discriminate now.

Three ratchets fired on a six-line change. loop.py's comment-density is frozen at 52.4 and may only fall; my added docstring took it to 52.6 and I walked it back to exactly 52.4 across three trims. loop.py now has 3 tokens of size headroom. tests/test_handoff_states.py crossed the 4000 cap, so the entry-refusal tests moved to tests/test_handoff_entry.py - their SECOND move for the same five tests, having come from test_handoff under basicly-kmqno2. And four docs citations naming loop.py line numbers went stale from an eight-line edit, which is basicly-e2mz.22 for the third time today.

Not done: the phase model question the record raised is untouched. A merge still happens outside the state that owns the artifact; this makes that merge honest rather than making it unnecessary.

Owner decision 2026-08-20 on basicly-7phc: cut before the loop and board work lands, because the release workflow reads CHANGELOG.md from the tagged commit and every unreleased fragment is a one-shot risk. That cut never happened. On 2026-08-28 main holds 903 commits and 150 changelog fragments since v0.9.0, including two BREAKING removals (the code-reviewer agent, the external tracker binary). Owner decision 2026-08-28: cut v0.10.0 from main as it stands, before any further landing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `uv run basicly release 0.10.0 --issue <this-id> --dry-run` runs on a clean main with both verify modes witnessed, IT SHALL report zero blocking reasons and list every fragment under changelog.d.
- WHEN the release runs, `CHANGELOG.md` SHALL carry a `## v0.10.0 - 2026-08-28` section holding every fragment, `changelog.d/` SHALL be empty, `__version__` SHALL read `0.10.0`, and the annotated tag `v0.10.0` SHALL point at the release commit.
- WHEN `git push origin main` and `git push origin v0.10.0` run, the release workflow SHALL go green and the GitHub release body SHALL equal the tagged CHANGELOG section.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/__init__.py`
- `CHANGELOG.md`
- `changelog.d/**`
- `README.md`
- `site/index.html`
- `.scripts/bootstrap.*`

## Plan

- demonstration: `git tag -l v0.10.0` prints the tag and `gh release view v0.10.0` prints the body.

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-27 on `basicly-6ajmrc`: the landing failed `pyright-windows`, and the repair brief at `.basicly/usage/repair-brief.json` carried `"evidence": [{"check": "verify full", "command": "basicly verify --mode full", "output": ""}]`; `verify-run.json` recorded `"detail": ""` for the failing check. The next session had to re-run the check by hand to learn the two errors. The ledger shows the pattern repeats: 35 landings failed `verify full` (pytest 44, lint-imports 24, docs-claims 16 by check), and the finding-set warning "the gate reported the same 2 finding(s) as the previous attempt ... this round changed nothing it reports" appears on lint-imports rounds, which is what a repair briefed with no output looks like.

The output exists at the moment it is dropped. `merge.py` re-runs the failures with `verify.rerun_failures(report, worktree_path, verify_mode, capture=True)` for its unreliable-gate test, so `rerun.results[*].output` holds the transcript; `MergeResult` keeps a one-line `detail` and the transcript is discarded. `loop._landing_verify_evidence` documents the gap in its own docstring ("Only the command, not the output ... widening it is merge's contract to change").

## Steps to Reproduce

In a worktree bound to a lane, introduce a type error that only `pyright --pythonplatform Windows` reports, commit, run `basicly loop advance <id>` from base. Observed: the landing fails, the brief's `evidence[0].output` is `""`. Expected: `evidence` holds one entry per failing check with the check's captured stdout+stderr, clipped from the front to the configured brief length.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a landing whose re-run reproduces N failing checks when the repair brief is written then `evidence` holds N entries, each naming the check, its command, and the captured output of the re-run.
- Given a failing check when `verify-run.json` is written then its `detail` holds the check's captured output or a one-line reason, never an empty string for a `fail` status.
- Given a landing with an unreliable or foreign verdict when the brief is written then no evidence entry is fabricated for it (behaviour unchanged).
- Demonstrated by: `uv run pytest tests/test_loop.py tests/test_merge.py tests/test_repair_brief.py -q` with a test that lands a worktree carrying a failing check and reads the captured output back out of the brief.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/repair_brief.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_repair_brief.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

The 46 `evidence` mentions in those modules are all `repair_brief.verify_evidence` (tests/test_repair_brief.py:64-97), the pre-existing in-place-repair path, not `loop._landing_evidence`. The test that actually lands a worktree carrying a failing check is tests/test_loop_repair_evidence.py::test_a_landing_briefs_its_repair_with_the_output_the_gate_captured, in a module the declared command does not name — the commit message says the ratchet forced test additions into new sibling modules, and the acceptance criterion was never updated to follow them. This also weakens the fragment's universal 'each failing check's own command and captured output' for the same N; I looked for a cap test and for a qualifier in the fragment and found neither.

unsupported.claim: instead of the whole-suite command and an empty string
unsupported.why: Read as unconditional it is false on one reachable path. src/basicly/merge.py:332 returns `MergeResult(name, "verify-failed", detail) if owed else None` with no `checks=`, unlike the two sites at merge.py:359 and merge.py:366 which the diff amended to pass `checks=_failed_checks(rerun)`. payload.description:
## Context

Found by the lane-C survey 2026-08-14.

```text
fragment.schema.json   restates schema.CATEGORIES (13 values), PRIORITY_MAP keys,
                       STATUSES, and the source enum
skill.schema.json      restates the invocation vocabulary from skill_source.py:44-46
agent.schema.json:58   restates the source enum
```

Exactly one of these pairs carries a tripwire. `tests/test_catalog_lint.py:372-377` binds the agent `tier` enum to `schema.MODEL_TIERS`, and `schema.py:66-67` documents that as the pattern.

## Consequence

A category added to `schema.py:21-37` and not to the JSON enum makes core sources fail lint while overlays pass, because an overlay is validated only by `loader._validate_fragment`. That core and overlay split is what produced `basicly-axqe` for tiers.

## Measured

`rg -n 'CATEGORIES|STATUSES|PRIORITY_MAP' tests/test_catalog_lint.py tests/test_loader.py tests/test_schema.py` returns nothing. The positive control, the same probe form for `MODEL_TIERS`, finds `tests/test_catalog_lint.py:372`.

## Acceptance

- When a JSON schema under the catalog restates an enum that exists as a Python constant, then the suite fails if the two sets differ.
- When a new enum pair is added, then it is covered by the same parametrised test rather than by a new one.

## Scope

- `tests/test_catalog_lint.py`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/` read only

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_catalog_lint.py -q`, with a deliberate one-value divergence proving the test fails.
payload.title: a json schema restates a python enum and only one pair is tripwired

payload.description:
From spike basicly-zv48 dimension 2. Captured runner stdout/stderr is never inspected/filtered/egress-limited. Redact secrets from persisted/surfaced runner output and optionally assert a network-restricted sandbox for headless runs.

Investigation (2026-07-18): run_record.py already never persists output (only a redacted command), so the gap is the surfaced/live RunResult.stdout/stderr, emitted raw by the CLI runner run and read by the loop/rubrics. The yzyd secret-scan hook (.basicly/core/hooks/secret-scan.py) has a high-signal pattern set to reuse, but it is a standalone stdlib hook (not importable), so a sibling redact module in src/basicly mirrors its patterns. Egress: basicly cannot portably network-sandbox a generic subprocess; that is agent-layer (codex sandbox = basicly-t0kt, claude/copilot config), so this task documents the egress posture rather than building a speculative seam (user-scoped 2026-07-18).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new redact module redacts high-signal secret patterns (private-key header, aws/github/slack/google/openai tokens, slack webhook, and the generic secret-named assignment with placeholder filtering) from arbitrary text, replacing each hit with a labeled placeholder; secret-free text is returned unchanged.
- runner.run applies redaction to captured stdout and stderr so every surfaced/persisted RunResult carries redacted output (guardrail at the source); dry-run and handoff results (empty output) are unaffected.
- The redaction patterns mirror the secret-scan hook (basicly-yzyd) as the sibling detector, noted in a comment so the two stay in step.
- Egress is documented as delegated to the agent-layer sandbox (codex basicly-t0kt, claude/copilot config); basicly redacts output but does not sandbox a generic subprocess. No speculative seam is added.
- Deterministic tests cover each secret pattern class, secret-free passthrough, and run() redacting both stdout and stderr.
payload.title: Guardrails: runner output secret-redaction plus egress-policy seam

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-ua9o5g` gave the board a region that draws a pending ask with the exact command and a prefilled form. It reads `asks[].actions[].basicly` to know which verb an ask offers.

**This producer never writes that key.** So the region is correct and unfed: on a real board it draws nothing, whatever is pending.

## Measured

```text
$ grep -c '"actions"' src/basicly/board_sections.py
0
$ grep -l '"actions"' src/basicly/board_asks.py src/basicly/board_regions.py
src/basicly/board_asks.py
src/basicly/board_regions.py
```

The zero is a controlled one: the same pattern finds both consumers, so it is absence and not a wrong probe. `board_sections.asks` builds `wait_id`, `kind`, `requested_at`, `issue`, `waiting_s`, and optionally `subject` and `question` — read the whole function; there is no `actions` branch.

Three fixtures (`wall-v1`, `dense-v1`, `full-v1`) carry `actions` because they were hand-authored against the schema. That is why `tests/test_board_action_wire.py` passes while the live board draws no form: its document is a fixture with the key supplied.

## Why it is one line of judgement, not one line of code

The verb is derivable from the ask's own `kind`, which `policy.record_wait_request` writes: `checkpoint` is answered by `policy checkpoint --approve`, `decision` by `loop answer`. What must not happen is a default — an ask of an unrecognised kind must carry no `actions`, so the schema's *"drawn without a button rather than refused"* rule applies rather than the board offering a verb that does not fit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the producer emits an ask of kind `checkpoint`, IT SHALL carry one action offering `checkpoint-approve`.
- WHEN it emits an ask of kind `decision`, IT SHALL carry one action offering `loop-answer`.
- WHEN it emits an ask of any other kind, IT SHALL carry no `actions` key at all, and the consumer SHALL still draw the ask in the watch band.
- WHEN the board is served with a real pending checkpoint, THE PAGE SHALL carry a prefilled form for it — demonstrated against a live board, not a fixture.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_board_sections.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: Queue a real checkpoint, serve the board, and read the form off the served page.

payload.description:
When an agent runs a positive control and it returns zero, I want the rule to say what the control must be built from, so I can stop reading a control's own zero as confirmation.

Asked for by the terminal canary as term-2vkce, and the request is well founded: the rule is in managed core they may never edit, they followed both halves of it, and still got a false reading. The wording said run a positive control and that if the control is empty too the zero belongs to the probe. It never said what the control must be built from.

Their case is the evidence. They planted a table they called ragged; it was valid compact style, so it was never a violation, reported zero, and read exactly like a dead probe. Rebuilt from the defect actually observed - padded cells over an unpadded delimiter row - it reported two errors. What rescued the diagnosis was the denominator: 151 files became 152 when the control was added, which proved the file was read and sent them to the table rather than the tooling.

Three of my own false zeros the same day were the environment answering instead of the code. Theirs is the subtler one and the one the rule did not cover.

Carrying it in their overlay was the fallback, and the objection to that is right: two copies of one rule drift, and ours is the copy every other consumer reads.
